Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART TWO: Man City's formidable start under Enzo Maresca, how Hull have shocked the league and Spurs and Man United struggle - last 10 sides GRADED
Sports.content:
The beginning of the new Premier League season has been scintillating to say the least with fans going through every possible emotion during the opening five gameweeks. While Manchester City and Arsenal being in the top two at this early stage is no great surprise, the league has had its fair share of unpredictability, with Spurs being bottom and Manchester United failing to take advantage of their kind start on paper. The newly promoted sides all look to pose a decent threat to the weaker sides – especially Hull, who have lost just once so far. The extended international break gives us time to take stock and review how clubs have got on. Daily Mail Sport has already graded the first ten teams – now it is the time for a verdict on the rest. Hull City Position: 8th. Points: 8 The first team to receive their grade in part two are the roaring Tigers, who have been electric upon their return to the Premier League. Many wrote this Hull team off before a ball was even kicked, deeming the squad too weak and the manager too inexperienced to have any chance of staying up. But after a ten-year hiatus from the Premier League, Jakirovic's men have looked more like European hopefuls rather than relegation fodder so far. They made a perfect start to the campaign by beating Manchester United and have kept up steady form since, seeing off fellow newcomers Coventry away and earning creditable draws against Chelsea and Aston Villa. Hull have found success through solidity and ruthless finishing – they were also the last side this season to concede a goal – and have outperformed their xG in every one of their wins this season. Defeat at Newcastle remains their only blip so far and, while it will be tough for Hull to maintain their early form and retain their top-flight status, they are already proving their doubters wrong. Grade: A Hull continue to surprise with the newly-promoted side losing only one of their opening five Ipswich Town Position: 11th. Points: 6 Another newly promoted team are up next. Ipswich Town have made a swift return to the Premier League at the first time of asking after relegation in 2024/25 - and look better equipped this time around. Under Gary O'Neil – sacked by Wolves after losing to his current club in late 2024 – they have made a promising start to their campaign as they bid to avoid dropping back into the Championship. Ipswich sit comfortably in 11th place at the first break of the season after two impressive victories over two sides that may also be battling for survival, Sunderland and Crystal Palace. Defeats at Old Trafford and at home to Liverpool were to be expected and are not the games O'Neil and his progressive, attacking side will be judged on come what May. If they maintain this level they have every chance of staying up. Grade: B+ Rolling over the competition: The Tractor boys are loving life back in the big leagues Leeds United Position: 5th. Points: 9 Yet another surprise package this season are Leeds, who have looked a huge threat so far this season. Dominic Calvert-Lewin's three goals in the first five matches have helped propel Daniel Farke's unbeaten side into the early European places. This has been no fluke either – Leeds have been playing some of the best football in the division with a five-man midfield that has the capacity to dominate proceedings. An impressive demonstration of their style came in a 4-1 rout of Newcastle, with three goals coming without reply in the first half. The season is still at a very, very early stage but Farke's start, coupled with the smart business done in the transfer window, will have fans dreaming of more than a relegation battle and perhaps an outside push for a European place. Leeds will return from the international break to the toughest of tests, a lunchtime kick-off at Arsenal. Most will assume the Gunners will end their unbeaten run but don't bet against an upset at the Emirates. Grade: A Daniel Farke has experienced some tough seasons in the Premier League before but now could have something special brewing at Elland Road Liverpool Position: 6th. Points: 9 Mixed results early on may have left supporters wondering where to stand on Andoni Iraola's start to life at Anfield. Following a dismal defence of their Premier League crown last season, leading to the sacking of Arne Slot, Iraola has arrived with fresh ideas and a new plan – which even he has admitted is tricky for his expensive band of stars. After the departure of Mo Salah in the summer, there are now only three players from Jurgen Klopp's legendary Premier League and Champions league winning side and finding replacements have been an expensive and largely unsuccessful process for Liverpool so far. But, after the issues of the 2025-26 campaign, Iraola has managed to get a tune out of some Liverpool's big money recruits. Alexander Isak is finally firing after returning from a nasty injury, Alexis Mac Allister is back to his best despite his contract dispute and Cody Gakpo has transformed his game. These improvements have helped Liverpool to remain unbeaten in the first five but draws with Forest, Newcastle and Fulham will be a worry. They have also been left defensively exposed in midfield at times and are yet to see a return of investment from £116million Florian Wirtz. Iraola will only grow into the role but, as the schedule gets tighter and tougher tests await, Liverpool will be hoping that doesn't take too long. Grade: B Alexander Isak is back in the goals and unbeaten Liverpool will hope Iraola can get this team of superstars finally ticking Manchester City Position: 1st. Points: 15 The only 100 per cent side so far are of course the perennial title challengers, Manchester City. City have adapted marvellously to life under Enzo Maresca. Worryingly for the rest, the former Chelsea boss appears to have picked up from where Pep Guardiola left off in the club's first season in a decade without the Spaniard at the helm. Erling Haaland has begun another campaign in splendid form, sitting at the top of the goalscoring charts with five in five games, and will hope his goals can bring the title back to the Etihad after two years, the longest it has been away from City since Guardiola's arrival in 2016. As always the owners splashed the cash in the summer, spending £321million to build a new midfield in the wake of legends Bernardo Silva, Ilkay Gundogan and Rodri all leaving. The investment already seems to be paying off. Elliot Anderson has started to look very accomplished at the base of Maresca's double pivot in midfield, the young Ayyoub Bouaddi has been impressively comfortable in a new league and Enzo Fernandez has been magnificent following his move from Chelsea. Arsenal will have a tough job on their hands stopping this City juggernaut from rolling towards what would be a ninth Premier League title but considering the start both teams have had we can be excited for another close and chaotic title race. Grade: A Manchester City are already firing under Maresca with five wins from five leaving them top Manchester United Position: 12th. Points: 5 From the blue half of Manchester to the red – and completely differing fortunes for United, who have endured a woeful start to the campaign. A kind start to the season, featuring games against two newly-promoted sides, has not yielded the results Michael Carrick, the club and the fans would have wanted or expected. The Red Devils got off to the worst possible start with defeat at Hull and haven't fully recovered since. They managed to respond the following week with an emphatic 5-2 win over Ipswich but that remains their only league victory so far this season. Carrick was trusted with the permanent role in the summer after an excellent end to last season but teams already seem to have worked his style out. Opponents appear to have got wise to his counter-attacking style and his players have struggled to break down opponents, while failing to keep clean sheets. Many feel the club's recruitment team left Carrick short in the summer window and the Red Devils are feeling the effects now. Unless these underlying issues with tactics and personnel are sorted, United are in danger of slipping back down the table and starting the process of a 'rebuild' all over again. Grade: D Manchester United have made a poor start to a season that had promised so much Newcastle United: Position: 9th. Points: 8 After a summer of being gutted Matthias Jaissle has done remarkably well to steady the ship at St James' Park. The Magpies had a testing transfer window losing not only Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes but also their long-term manager Eddie Howe and have incredibly rolled with the punches perhaps looking even better as a result. Young German coach Matthias Jaissle has come in and instilled the same style of play that Jurgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel found so much success with in England and is taking Newcastle into a new era. Of course they have not been perfect on Tyneside but considering what some Geordies feared I think they will be pleased with the steady progress they have made in the first month. The Magpies did take a real wing clipping against Leeds losing 4-1 away at Elland road but that aside results have been steady. They have had drawn two all twice at home and managed wins against Spurs and Hull, being the first side this season to pick up three points against the Tigers and appear to score in bunches with their goals coming within less than ten minutes of each other in both their wins. Grade: B Geordies will be extremely pleased with their start to season after a rough summer and look forward to the Premier League returning more than most Nottingham Forest Position: 13th. Points: 5 Oliver Glasner was tasked with being the man to provide stability to Nottingham Forest after the club churned through four managers last season, which began with Nuno Espirito Santo's acrimonious departure. Glasner's side are yet to truly get going so far this campaign, something that might concern their ambitious owner Evangelos Marinakis. Concerningly, Forest have failed to score in their three home matches against Leeds, Tottenham and Coventry, losing two of them. The 1-0 defeat to newly promoted Coventry – who had lost their opening four matches without scoring – will have worried fans heading into the extended international break. Forest's sole league win came away against midlands rivals Aston Villa, with Igor Jesus's late goal giving them their highlight of the campaign to date. Grade: C Forest will need to pick up regular points quickly to avoid slipping further down the table after the international break Sunderland Position: 14th. Points: 4 The Black Cats have the tricky task of backing up their stunning campaign last season after their promotion back to the top flight, which ended in Europa League qualification. Few are expecting them to kick on this campaign, with a drop off considered more likely due to having to balance European football with their domestic endeavours. Sunderland have only managed one win so far against a struggling Fulham side, but have also had to face both Manchester City and Arsenal in the first month. They performed well in both but ultimately suffered defeats, despite Brian Brobbey's hat-trick at the Etihad. Regis Le Bris's men will be frustrated to have slipped up in their season opener away at Ipswich where they lost late on to the hands of their former player, Jack Clarke. Four points may be seen as a disappointing return to date, with the fixture list only going to become more congested and the squad stretched after the international break. Grade: C+ Sunderland have been unlucky thus far but must begin winning again soon if they are to avoid the common second season relegation Tottenham Hotspur Position: 20th. Points: 2 After back-to-back 17th placed finishes, Tottenham's heavy summer spending prompted hope they could lift themselves out of the crisis state the club has been in. Yet Tottenham find themselves propping up the table after five games with Roberto De Zerbi's side still without a win in the league. Spurs have only managed two goals all season and are sat rudderless at the bottom of the table Most pundits believe Tottenham have too much quality to get involved in another relegation scrap, but their start to the season has been extremely worrying. Tottenham have proved unable so far to resolve their disastrous home record that has plagued them over the past two seasons. De Zerbi's side have been beaten by Newcastle and Aston Villa – who both underwent drastic summer changes as well – and also drew with Everton in front of their home fans. The club's ownership has so far yet to see the return on the more than £300million spent on new arrivals this summer, after they reacted to the scare of just surviving on the final day of last season. A major improvement in results after the international break is needed to lift the mood and ensure Tottenham are not facing a third consecutive season of struggle at the wrong end of the table. Grade: F

Sports.title: Why Tottenham may regret selling red-hot Will Lankshear, the warning signs Lee Carsley cannot ignore and a fresh Chelsea injury concern as England's Under 21s beat Kazakhstan 4-2
Sports.content:
England men's Under 21s squeezed past Kazakhstan to move Lee Carsley's side within one match of sealing their place at next summer's tournament.

The back-to-back reigning champions made life difficult for themselves, going behind early on and then conceding an equaliser on the stroke of half-time.

But goals from Manchester City loanee Max Alleyne and former Tottenham striker Will Lankshear ensured England picked up all three points in a dominant qualifying campaign in which the Young Lions have won eight and drawn one of their nine matches.

England now need just a point against Slovakia next Friday to seal their spot as one of the 16 sides heading to Albania and Serbia next year.

Daily Mail Sport's TARA ANSON-WALSH was at Molineux Stadium to give you the things we learned from England's 4-2 win over Kazakhstan...

Lee Carsley's side now need just one point against Slovakia next Friday to book their spot among the 16 sides heading to Albania and Serbia next year

The striker Tottenham let get away

The name on everyone's lips at the moment is former Tottenham striker Will Lankshear after the 21-year-old's impressive start to the season at Middlesbrough.

Lankshear joined Boro for £20million this summer after making six appearances for Spurs during the 2024-25 season, scoring once. He has hit the ground running on Teesside, scoring six times in his first eight Championship matches.

His purple patch showed no signs of slowing on Friday, with the forward sliding in to score an impressive flick from close range just 22 minutes after coming off the bench.

England have produced plenty of No10s in recent years, winning the 2025 Euros without a recognised centre forward, but the lack of an out-and-out striker has long been a bugbear for Carsley.

Michael Owen even suggested Lankshear should have been considered by Thomas Tuchel amid a 'dearth' of strikers in the game and no obvious successor to Harry Kane.

Carsley, mindful of not overhyping a youngster who has already begun to draw comparisons with England's record goalscorer, was measured in his praise at full-time.

'He's had a strong week. The way he's played at Middlesbrough, he's definitely brought that confidence into the camp.

'You always wonder whether that's transferrable, when you're doing so well at a club, but he's showed that tonight. His finish was outstanding.

'He's shown a bit of character because I left him out of the squad for the first game against Kazakhstan (last September) and sometimes that goes one way or the other and he's definitely found his game.'

As for Tottenham, given their own struggles in front of goal this season, Roberto De Zerbi and Co may yet come to regret cashing in on a young striker who cannot stop finding the back of the net.

Lankshear's purple patch showed no signs of slowing on Friday, with the forward sliding in to score from close range just 22 minutes after coming off the bench

Man City's academy shines amid the chaos

On the day news broke that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges, three City academy graduates lined up for Carsley's side, more than from any other club.

Those were Rico Lewis, Under 21 debutant Stephen Mfuni (on loan at Coventry City) and goalscorer Max Alleyne (on loan at Birmingham City). Divin Mubama, who is currently on loan at Southampton, completed the City contingent, although he is not an academy graduate, having come through the ranks at West Ham.

For everything that has clearly been wrong with how the club has been managed over the past couple of decades, that cannot detract from the plaudits it deserves for its investment in local talent.

Appearing unfazed by the latest developments, the trio impressed in equal measure against Kazakhstan. Lewis looked particularly strong going forward and consistently looks at ease in this expansive set-up. Mubama provided a serious goal threat and was unlucky not to score in the first half. And centre back Alleyne capped off his night with his first Under 21s goal on the hour mark, guiding home the winner from a free kick.

City's Lewis looked particularly strong going forward and consistently looks at ease in this expansive set-up

Carsley gets a timely warning

For all England's dominance, this match against the group's underdogs was not without its concerns for Carsley.

Kazakhstan had not scored more than once in any of their previous nine qualifying matches and ended that two-year run at Molineux on Friday night.

The manner of the goals conceded will be Carsley's chief concern given they both came from moments when England appeared to be sleeping at set pieces.

Kazakhstan's first arrived after just three minutes from a corner, and it quickly became apparent that Carsley's side had not realised the game had started when Artyom Litosh breezed into the six-yard box and coolly volleyed home to send the 20 or so away fans, four of whom stood proudly behind a Kazakhstan flag for most of the match, into raptures.

The visitors' equaliser before the break came from a long throw, with Kazakhstan's Saif Popov given two attempts at goal before his third effort finally found a way past Birmingham City's James Beadle.

Not only that, but England also looked vulnerable immediately after scoring two of their goals and would have been punished had Kazakhstan possessed a little more quality.

At full time, Carsley said: 'This team haven't played together for six months, so I'm not going to be too critical, but they know that they have to play better than that if we're going to be a serious team.

'We were too open at times. Against a better team, no disrespect to Kazakhstan... we were under pressure.'

Kazakhstan had not scored more than once in any of their previous nine qualifying matches and ended that two-year run at Molineux on Friday night

Fresh frustration for Gittens

What had already appeared to be a difficult start to the season for Jamie Gittens now looks as though it may have become even tougher.

After making 16 appearances for Chelsea last term, Gittens has yet to feature for Xabi Alonso's side in the Premier League, with his only two outings this season coming in the Carabao Cup.

Any hopes of breaking into the first-team picture may now be delayed further after the 22-year-old limped off in the 39th minute following a kick to the ankle and headed straight down the tunnel.

He later left the stadium on crutches and wearing a protective boot, with Carsley confirming he will return to the London club for a full assessment.

Gittens left the stadium on crutches and wearing a protective boot, with Carsley confirming he will return to his club for a full assessment

A homecoming for Coady

Sometimes football's storylines are simply too neat, and Conor Coady's return to Molineux for his first taste of coaching with the Under 21s was one of them.

The 33-year-old agreed to terminate his contract with Wrexham in the summer before being swiftly appointed as Carsley's assistant. Coady has not formally retired, either, with Carsley joking that his ability to still join in training is 'a bonus'.

'He's an excellent example,' Carsley said. 'It's always important that we have someone on the staff who knows what it's like to play at Wembley for England and to be around squads. We had that in Ash (Ashley Cole) and Joleon (Lescott) and now we've got it in Conor.'

Coady received a warm welcome on his return to Molineux, where he spent seven seasons marshalling Wolves' defence. The Liverpudlian's 314 appearances for the club still place him among the club's top 20 appearance-makers of all time.

Sports.title: Former Liverpool star Andy Robertson admits 'shock' over Man City's guilty verdict in case against Premier League - but insists players who beat him to TWO titles are not to blame
Sports.content:
Scotland captain Andy Robertson insists it would be wrong for Manchester City’s players to be tarnished by the bombshell verdict on the club’s breach of financial regulations.

City have finally been found guilty on almost all of the 115 charges which had been hanging over them for these past few years.

During his nine years as a Liverpool player, Robertson jousted regularly with City as the two clubs forged one of the great rivalries in the Premier League era.

Robertson was twice part of a Liverpool side that finished second to City in the Premier League in 2019 and 2022. But, in terms of the players he faced on the pitch, Robertson insists he holds no grudges after some epic battles with City over the years.

‘I think you can hear the shock in my voice,’ said Robertson, who will lead Scotland out and win his 98th cap in the Nations League clash against Slovenia.

‘The case has obviously been going on. For me, the [Man City] players showed they were good enough on the pitch.

Andy Robertson was involved in many fierce battles with Manchester City while at Liverpool

‘I don’t know too much about the charges. But they had an incredible team, one that I loved battling against.

‘I don’t think when it comes to these things that players are ever to blame. That’s all I can focus on.’

This will be the start of a new era for Scotland with Sebastien Pocognoli taking charge of the team for the first time.

Robertson revealed that the 39-year-old Belgian travelled to London to personally meet him and have dinner after being appointed.

The skipper is excited about the prospect of what the future could hold under the new head coach but also believes it’s important not to forget the achievements of Steve Clarke.

Clarke resigned after the World Cup in the summer following Scotland’s group stage exit, a fate they also suffered at Euro 2020 and Euro 2024.

‘Time will tell if it will look different,’ said Robertson. ‘We haven’t had a lot of time on the pitch. He’s given us good information without overloading us.

‘It’s been a really good training week. We’ve enjoyed it and hopefully that we can take that into this game against Slovenia.

Andy Robertson and Jack Hendry will hope to get Sebastien Pocognoli off to a positive start

‘I don’t think there’s an in-between. You can be excited for the future but respect the past. Some people have been caught in two minds on that.

‘In my opinion, the time under Steve Clarke was a hugely successful one. He came in and his remit was to qualify for tournaments. For him to do three out of four, that’s nothing but success.

‘We can talk about how we performed at the tournaments but as a team and as a country we managed to get back on the biggest stage.

‘That has to be a positive. Now, we can be excited for the future under this manager. It will maybe be a different way of playing, a different style, younger players coming in.

‘So you can do both. That would be my message to everyone. You can still appreciate what we had in the past and what we achieved. But we can also be excited for the future.

‘That’s been my message to the players and I think they can feel that. Hopefully we can push to reach new heights.’

Sports.title: Man City face RELEGATION 'nuclear option' and appeal 'highly unlikely to succeed', says their former financial advisor, as they are found guilty of 114 Premier League charges
Sports.content:
Former Manchester City financial advisor Stefan Borson has claimed 'anything is possible,' including the nuclear option of relegation, after the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

The Premier League accused the club of widespread financial cheating over an era of sustained success – with an independent panel hearing concluding in 2024.

There has since been a frustrating wait for a verdict but Daily Mail Sport sources have disclosed that clubs have been informed that the panel has now reached a decision – and there is a belief it's a win for the top flight.

City are understood to have been found guilty on all but one of their 115 rule-break charges concerning the Premier League’s financial regulations.

Borson, who advised Man City between 2002 and 2007, was asked by talkSPORT whether the nuclear option of relegation from the Premier League was on the table as a possible punishment following the decision.

'Anything is possible and all hell is now going to break loose, as this is going to go on for weeks and weeks and weeks,' Borson said.

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges

Former Man City financial advisor Stefan Borson believes 'anything is possible' regarding the club's potentinal punishments and that an appeal is 'hihgly unlikely to succeed'

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation

'It is going to be very hard for City to say anything or to contain the fallout from this scenario and that is without being able to see what is in this decision.

'We will almost certainly soon see the decision of the independent commission laid out in great detail, it will give people huge ammunition to attack those individuals and the club.

'Then we will go into the process, which will be behind closed doors, around the sanction.

'Man City have denied everything all the way through, they have gone through a process that may have cost more than £100m between the two parties and they have been found to have breached everything.

'They are in very, very serious trouble.'

An appeal from Man City is considered inevitable with the club having always strongly denied wrongdoing, since they were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: 'The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

'The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

Borson claimed an appeal from Man City is 'highly unlikely to succeed' and suggested their statement indicated their likely arguments in an attempt to overturn the verdict.

'An appeal on the facts is highly unlikely to succeed,' he said.

The club have maintained that they are innocent throughout the process and are expected to appeal

'Where we are now with City being found guilty of more or less everything, the decision itself will be scathing in terms of the club’s conduct, the conduct of individuals, the behaviour of individuals and the hearing itself in terms of their credibility. There won’t be any hiding place when that decision is published.

'To then have to present that to an appeal that does not have the benefit of listening to the whole case all over again, in terms of witness evidence, seeing all the documentation again, it is going to be extremely difficult for City to overturn those factual findings.

‘City have hinted in the last paragraph of their statement, I think their suggestion is that the process and panel itself was in some way partial and biased and that they will in some way challenge the length of time it has taken for the decision to come out.

'All of those sorts of arguments, be it bias or something procedural, all of them are very unlikely to succeed. Overturning factual findings I would say is very, very unlikely.

'Ultimately now I think City will have to take their punishment and it will be severe.'

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

A three-man panel was tasked with considering the evidence, with the initial expectation a verdict would have been reached on the case within months. It has since taken three-and-a-half years.

The original 115 charges were extended to a total of 130 after an administration issue in what is the most expensive and wide-ranging case in English football history.

Eight Premier League titles, three FA Cups, six League Cups and one Champions League have all been won by the club in the modern era

City remained steadfast in maintaining their innocence over more than 115 alleged breaches across eight years, some including the start of the Pep Guardiola era.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Between the years mentioned, Manchester City won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League, four FA Cups, and seven EFL Cups.

City vehemently denied any breaches of financial rules but the investigation started in December 2018 after German website Der Spiegel published documents from a Football Leaks cache which had originated from Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto.

It alleged that City had overstated sponsorship income with money paid from the club's owners instead of sponsors linked to Abu Dhabi.

Roberto Mancini's wages were said to have doubled via a secret contract with an Abu Dhabi club when he was at Man City, while they were also alleged to have broken rules over approaching young players.

The Mail on Sunday has led the way on reporting the story. In July 2021, they reported on emails that appeared to suggest that Man City had millions funnelled into the club by Abu Dhabi to help inflate their income.

Back in February 2020, the club were banned from the Champions League and fined £25million after they were found to have seriously misled European footballing governing body UEFA and broken financial fair play rules.

This was then lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport which also reduced the club's fine to £9million.

Sports.title: MAN CITY FAN VIEW: My club's relationship with financial skullduggery has left me yearning for the comedy club days, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
MAN CITY FAN VIEW: My club's relationship with financial skullduggery has left me yearning for the comedy club days, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

For those of us who supported Manchester City long before they were accused of financial skulduggery, it has been a strange few years.

City were completely inoffensive back then – the comedy club who once kept the ball near the corner flag because they had been (wrongly) told a draw would spare them relegation.

For years, the fans survived on scraps. The near miss in the 1981 FA Cup final, when they were robbed by a freakish Tommy Hutchison own goal. The Full Members’ Cup final of 1986, when they lost 5-4 to Chelsea. The mad play-off comeback against Gillingham.

But when the money poured in from Abu Dhabi, there arose a strange conundrum. Did I prefer the old days, when City were popular but useless? Or was it all about winning, no matter the cost? The answer was not always straightforward.

Now that they’ve been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges, at least we finally have a bit of clarity, grim though it looks.

My greatest fear has always been that they would be retrospectively stripped of titles, like Russian athletes at the Olympics.

Man City's 115 charges saga has left LAWRENCE BOOTH yearning for the comedy club days

The idea Sergio Aguero's last-gasp title winning goal against QPR in 2012 might now be null and void is hard to stomatch

Financial penalties, points deductions, even relegation – I could live with all that. But the idea that the last-ditch winner against QPR in 2011-12 might now be null and void is hard to stomach: Aguerooooo…oh!

Other fans, who have continually protested their indifference to a ‘small club’ like City, will still say their achievements deserve an asterisk. That’s how fandom operates. No matter the lawyers eventually conclude – needless to say, City will appeal – the court of public opinion made up its mind long ago.

I get the sentiment. I didn’t like the fact that City were attracting censure, not affection. I hated the thought that their trophies were regarded as ill-gotten gains. But try as I might, I couldn’t cut the umbilical cord. It’s not terribly logical, but that’s how fandom operates too.

I was also suspicious of the notion that money automatically means success. Manchester United are proof that life isn’t always so simple. Money helps, sure. But it has to be spent wisely: Sergio Aguero, Kevin de Bruyne, Bernardo Silva, Ederson, even Manuel Akanji – was anyone else trying to buy these guys?

Oddly, I found last season quite relaxing, what with Arsenal finally getting over the line. Sorry if it sounds arrogant, but winning the league was no longer the thrill it was when Aguero did his thing.

Life felt a bit more normal again: a draw was not a disaster, and City’s defending was occasionally comical, just like the old times. Who knows: perhaps, one day, people will even learn to love us again, though I accept that is more likely if we’re banished to the Enterprise Rent-A-Car National League first.

Sports.title: Rodri issues defiant response to Man City being found guilty of vast majority of Premier League rule break charges as former star insists he 'believes' in the club despite verdict
Sports.content:
Former Manchester City captain Rodri insists he 'believes in the club' and their success cannot be taken away after they were found guilty of the vast majority of their Premier League rule break charges.

Rodri, whose seven-year spell at Man City ended in the summer when he moved to Barcelona, became the first individual associated with the club to speak following the bombshell news on Friday.

Daily Mail Sport understands Man City were found guilty of all but one of their 115 charges by an independent panel.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties and even relegation.

Points deductions could even be applied onto previous seasons, raising the chance that City will be stripped of their Premier League titles.

When asked about the verdict ahead of Spain's Nations League match against England on Saturday, Rodri reiterated his belief Man City will be found innocent.

Rodri has insisted Man City's success cannot be taken away from them despite the club being found guilty of the majority their Premier League rule break charges

The former Man City captain insisted he believes in the innocence of the club amid the verdict

The midfielder referenced a previous 2020 decision which saw Man City banned from the Champions League and fined by UEFA for a breach of financial rules, which was later lifted on appeal by the Court of Arbitration for Sport which also reduced the club's fine to £9million.

'We have faced something similar in 2020 if I remember correctly, a similar process, a different accusation but similar process.

‘In the first instance we were found guilty but we believed in the club and the innocence the club maintained, and in the end we ended up being acquitted.

‘I believe in the justice system and I believe in the innocence of the club.’

When asked whether he had been given assurances by the club of their innocence, Rodri added: 'They always tell us the confidence of their innocence and when you look in someone’s eyes and they are talking in that way – and we have the example of 2020 the process was the same and at the end nothing happened – we were very calm in this way.

'We were never a team that was nervous about these kind of things. I am not going to say it is normal but some teams go through these situations and it is part of football today.

'Everyone has to follow the rules and for me that’s great. They always expressed the confidence they never did anything wrong and we believe in that, and that’s the thing.

'We will believe the club. I have been there and I know how they work and how they cooperate.'

Rodri insisted Man City's success was 'deserved' and the result of hard work from the players and staff

Rodri won four Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups, three Carabao Cups and a FIFA Club World Cup during a glittering spell at Man City under Pep Guardiola.

When asked whether he it hurt that Man City's achievements have been questioned, Rodri insisted the success of the players and staff during that period cannot be taken away.

'For us, the players, it is a different thing. For you guys there are all kinds of opinions but we always tried to think in a positive way,' Rodri said.

'When you live daily in that club and all the people that worked hard all these years to have all the success we have had, not only Pep [Guardiola] and the players, but from the owners to the guys that work daily, what we did they cannot take it out of us.

'It is not something that is paid by money, it is paid with effort and partnership, being shoulder to shoulder every day.

'We had a lot of success over the years and I can tell you that everything was deserved and I am glad I could live one of the best eras in English football.'

Man City are set to appeal the verdict.

A Manchester City spokesperson said: 'The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023.

'The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'

The club have maintained that they are innocent throughout the process and are expected to appeal

Man City, who have always strongly denied wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

Their statement that February insisted that they were 'surprised' by the charges.

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation. The alleged rule breaking was claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

A three-man panel was tasked with considering the evidence, with the initial expectation a verdict would have been reached on the case within months. It has since taken three-and-a-half years.

The original 115 charges were extended to a total of 130 after an administration issue in what is the most expensive and wide-ranging case in English football history.

City remained steadfast in maintaining their innocence over more than 115 alleged breaches across eight years, some including the start of the Pep Guardiola era.

The club were accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They were also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Sports.title: The clubs who could seek compensation as Premier League sides consider legal action after Man City found guilty of vast majority of rule breaches - and what happens next: Key questions answered
Sports.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their rule-break charges concerning the Premier League’s financial regulations.

The competition accused the club of widespread financial cheating over an era of sustained success – with an independent panel hearing concluding in 2024.

The long-awaited verdict has now been reached with the belief it is a victory for the Premier League, despite Man City having strenuously denied the charges.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation.

Daily Mail Sport's Mike Keegan provides answers to the key questions, including the next steps, Man City's expected appeal and how serious the punishment could be.

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 Premier League rule-break charges

WHAT DOES IT MEAN?

This cannot be viewed as anything other than an overwhelming victory for the Premier League.

To see Manchester City found guilty of the ‘vast majority’ of the 115 charges is an outcome that Richard Masters will no doubt see as vindication for what has been a costly, long-running legal battle in which the stakes were incredibly high.

It is safe to assume that had the tables turned the other way, the chief executive would have been in P45 territory.

More important than that, those who City feel were the key protagonists, the so-called ‘Red Cartel’, will also feel vindication.

To put it simply, Manchester City have been found guilty of cheating their way to success between 2009 and 2018, a period when they dominated English football.

The verdict cannot be viewed as anything other than an overwhelming victory for the Premier League and its chief executive Richard Masters

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

There has been no statement from the Premier League, while City’s only says that the process remains ongoing and is subject to strict confidentiality.

What is clear is that City will appeal. What is not clear is whether the sanction will drop before any appeal.

WHAT ARE THE PUNISHMENTS?

Take your pick. Hefty points deductions, potential relegation and transfer bans are all on the table. Rule W51 in the Premier League handbook states ambiguously that ‘such other penalty as it shall think fit’ is an option.

There is, however, a scepticism among some, based on a lack of noise from many of the other clubs and the lenient punishment recently handed to Chelsea that whatever penalty lands will not see City stripped of titles or relegated. ‘They’ll get a slap on the wrist and ordered to pay legal costs and not much else,’ one exec predicted.

The verdict could lead to a variety of punishments including huge points deductions, financial penalties, and even relegation

HOW DOES AN APPEAL WORK?

In all likelihood City will appeal and recent cases tell us that they tend to be dealt with expeditiously.

An appeal board would be set up, appointed by the chair of the panel and, again, featuring three people. Some feel that this would be an exercise in the Premier League marking its own homework.

At this early stage, it is worth an assumption that City could argue the panel was not impartial. The bad news for them, however, is that this is a high bar to clear.

Unlike City’s case with UEFA, it cannot go to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (who overturned UEFA’s findings).

WHAT ABOUT COMPENSATION?

Last year, in a move believed to have been instigated by former Arsenal chief executive Tim Lewis, the Gunners, Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Manchester United served legal notices reserving their right to take action.

Should the verdict stand, they will then seek damages for a wide variety of issues. The most costly claims are likely to come from those who say they missed out on Champions League qualification during the period in question thanks to City’s law breaking. But the scope would not end there.

Clubs could also, for example, argue that as a result of the breaches they were unable to sign a calibre of player that would have allowed them to be more successful on the field. Some believe £200m would not be out of the question, but that remains to be seen.

Ex-Arsenal chief executive is understood to have instigated a move last year that saw the Gunners, Tottenham, Liverpool and Man United served legal notices reserving their right to take action

WHAT ABOUT THE INDEPENDENT FOOTBALL REGULATOR?

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the Regulator declined to comment when contacted by Daily Mail Sport. However, David Kogan will be well aware of the situation.

The IFR was brought in for a variety of reasons, not least to ensure that those owning the nation’s football clubs were fit and proper to do so. The IFR would have the power to force City’s owners to sell, but such a scenario is viewed as unlikely.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

The Premier League and City are not commenting.

Given the verdict is in, the two parties will enter into a period of negotiation with regards to when the detail will be released. That will also include suggested redactions, as both sides go through what is likely to be a finding that may well run into the hundreds of pages.

DIDN’T CITY TRIUMPH OVER THE PREMIER LEAGUE RECENTLY ON SPONSORSHIP RULES?

They did, with three senior judges deeming the rules unlawful. As a result, a series of amendments were made. City again launched a legal challenge, but surprisingly came to an agreement with the Premier League in September. Those cases, however, were always separate to the 115, as it became known.

Sports.title: Argentina star Mauro Icardi hit with 73-YEAR driving ban after video posted online by his girlfriend alerted authorities to his expired driving licence
Sports.content:
Argentinian striker Mauro Icardi has been handed a remarkable 73-year driving ban for driving without a licence.

The former PSG and Inter Milan goal machine found himself in hot water after a video posted by Icardi's new girlfriend China Suarez caught the attention of the Argentine Ministry of Transport.

The video posted showed her hanging out of the window of a car driven by Icardi, just outside of Buenos Aires. The Ministry for Transport then launched an investigation which revealed the striker's driving licence had expired.

The Ministry have since published a statement on X saying: 'We found that Icardi's driving license had expired. For this reason, we have ordered his provisional disqualification... the player will need to be assessed to determine his fitness to drive. Road safety allows for no exception.'

The Ministry confirmed Icardi has been handed a driving ban until the end of the century.

The two-time Serie A golden boot winner issued a raunchy statement in response to the his suspension, writing: 'Think about fixing the roads to improve traffic flow instead of wasting time writing tweets and scratching your balls.'

Icardi has been a free agent since leaving Galatasaray and had links to Spurs in the summer but now has a new issue on his hands

The striker began dating China Saurez (left) shortly after his divorce from famous WAG Wanda Nara last year

The striker is now locked in a battle against the ministry challenging the suspension with the hope of having it lifted.

As part of his punishment Icardi also has also had his Italian driving licence cancelled despite it being valid until 2029.

The striker again took to social media to voice his displeasure, writing: 'I want to know how you have managed cancel my Italian driving licence.'

The striker is no stranger to controversy off the pitch having been embroiled in one of the most famous footballing scandals.

In 2013, after first joining Inter Milan, fellow Argentinian Maxi Lopez welcomed the then 19-year-old to Italy by frequently inviting him to his house to meet his family and enjoy time off together and over time Icardi privately grew close to Lopez's then wife Wanda Nara.

Lopez and Nara eventually separated in late 2013 and shockingly a year later Nara tied the knot with Icardi.

Both Nara and Icardi repeatedly denied their relationship had begun before her divorce from Lopez.

Yet the perceived betrayal had led to the striker being kept out of the Argentine national team for most of his early career due to the scrutiny he received.

Nara and Icardi endured an acrimonious separation early last year and begun dating his new girlfriend China Suarez but remains in litigation with Nara over the pair's divorce settlement.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
