Sports.title: Why "dangerous" Hamilton-Lawson incident in Azerbaijan GP practice hasn't led to change
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton was reprimanded for impeding Liam Lawson during Thursday's second practice in FP2 but this wasn't the end of the matter.

Even before a single car had turned a wheel on the Baku City Circuit, concerns had been raised about how cars running slowly to harvest or conserve electrical energy through the final corners could represent a hazard to those on a push lap.

In previous years, even those cars not trying to set a timed lap would travel reasonably quickly through Turns 16-19, a left-hander followed by two kinks leading onto the main straight. But the need to preserve electrical power for the straight means there are now huge disparities in speed between those pushing through this area and those just about to open a full-send lap.

The incident between Hamilton and Lawson was a textbook example of what the drivers had feared: Hamilton was on an out-lap, and had been warned Lawson was approaching on a flying lap. Hamilton thought he had enough margin but was caught out because, in the present generation of cars, the amount of electrical boost available is governed by software.

In this case, the driver cannot command full power until the car arrives at a predetermined point on the main straight – otherwise the battery would begin to deplete and enter the ‘ramp-down' phase too early, costing top speed.

"I could see him, I thought the gap was enough, I got to full throttle," Hamilton said after FP2. "Literally as I got into [Turn] 18, the car just died. Swamped up the gap massively and that could happen to anyone."

The need to preserve battery levels for the long straight has made the preceding corners potentially dangerous Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

At the time, Lawson, who had to swerve to avoid the slow-moving Ferrari, took to the radio to emote vociferously: ""Oh my god, that is so f****** dangerous," he complained.

Once the adrenaline had subsided, Lawson agreed with Hamilton.

"There's not really a lot you can do when you look at it," he said. "Lewis comes out of [Turn] 16 in his full throttle, he's got two or three seconds to me which is normally plenty of gap but the speed difference is just so big. He's not deploying anything, I'm deploying everything and you have 60, 70, 80 km/h speed difference, which is bad.

"The problem is if he gets out of the way before 18 and slows down, if there's another car behind me then the speed difference is enormous. So it's something we have to look at overnight.

"If there's something we can do, it's going to have to be before 16 honestly because once you come out of that corner and you're committed."

Ahead of the weekend, race director Rui Marques set out clear guidelines in his regular briefing document for how drivers should tackle this section.

"Cars on out-laps or slow laps should keep extreme left (i.e. not "offline" in middle of track) from exit T16 through to entry T18," said the competition notes.

Drivers on out-laps are instructed to stay on the "extreme left" of the track after Turn 16 Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

"We consider that teams/drivers can and should manage traffic gaps before T18 (going as slowly as required being on the extreme left) to ensure that they can transit between the apex of T18 and apex of T19 without impeding an approaching car that is trying to set a competitive lap time.

"Cars on out-laps or slow laps should keep "extreme" right exit T19 until they achieve relevant speed to open the following lap."

Among the reasons for Hamilton receiving a reprimand after the FP2 incident was that he had failed to obey the instruction to stay on the extreme left. But he felt that a better solution was required – perhaps to enable drivers to have access to more power through that section.

"We'll talk about it in the drivers briefing, about what we could do," he said.

"What they should do is on a single lap, when we're doing a pushing lap, we get max power out of the last corner. When you come through 19 [the final kink before the straight section], it resets, and then you have a little bit more power than the other car.

"There should just be nobody going slow ever through 18 and 19. Even if you're on a slow lap, you still have to go flat out through 18 and 19 with full power. That would mean no one's ever going slow through that section."

Autosport understands that this was indeed discussed during Thursday night's drivers' briefing, but was ultimately vetoed by the teams. The scenario is similar to that in the season-opening Australian Grand Prix weekend, when Turn 9 on the Albert Park circuit was described by the drivers as "sketchy" under the new technical regulations, because it came at the end of one of five straightline mode (SLM) zones where the cars' active aerodynamics are deployed.

Ahead of FP3, the FIA announced it was removing that SLM zone, only to have to revert to the original format after pushback from the teams. There, as in Azerbaijan this weekend, the rationale was understood to be technical and performance-related: removing that SLM zone would undo all the work the teams had done to plan their energy management.

As such, the race director's original "keep left" instructions will stand for FP3 and qualifying in Baku.

Sports.title: Imola or Qatar and Abu Dhabi? What’s really going on with the end of the 2026 F1 season
Sports.content:
As Formula 1 enters the final phase of the season, with three triple-headers on paper, the question remains where the 2026 season will end. In theory, the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix are still scheduled to take place, and F1 strongly emphasises that, as things stand, this also remains plan A.

At the same time, F1 has to be prepared for a scenario in which those races have to be cancelled because of all the continued unrest in the Middle East, and so the green light has been given behind the scenes to work on a plan B. Unsurprisingly, that plan B is the Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari.

Sources within F1 told Autosport that the organisers in Imola have now been given the green light to build the grandstands and make preparations as if the race in Emilia-Romagna will take place.

This does not mean it will actually happen – Qatar and Abu Dhabi still constitute plan A – but Formula One Management (FOM) has to press ahead with an alternative in order to guarantee a season finale after the Las Vegas Grand Prix in any scenario.

Building the grandstands and continuing all preparations without final confirmation of a race logically brings financial risks, but sources in the paddock say F1 is covering all those risks. This means F1 is fully paying for the preparations – including the construction of the temporary grandstands – and that Imola will not face any financial risk regardless of the outcome.

In the scenario that the Imola option ultimately proves unnecessary, this approach will cost F1 money, but the sport has no choice. After all, if the situation in the Middle East escalates further a month before the scheduled races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, F1 cannot afford not to have a plan B ready to go.

This also underlines that F1 wants to wait as long as possible before making a final decision, while it should not be forgotten how financially attractive the final two race weekends in the Middle East are.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali initially said a decision would be made in mid-September, but the situation has changed since then.

Several team principals currently point to mid-October as the new timeframe for clarity, although F1 stresses that there is no hard deadline. From a logistical perspective, there is still relatively little urgency at this stage, as long as Imola is fully ready to step in on the first weekend of December.

The teams have also been informed of this reality and are not particularly concerned for now, several team principals stressed during Thursday’s press conference in Baku.

“I believe that Stefano was targeting to tell us in mid-October, right? So, we all know what the situation is”, Haas team boss Ayao Komatsu said.

“I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it. I think the challenges are, for instance, things like European motorhome structure, etcetera. All those people who look after them, they have a winter job, so we need to find alternative people to do that.

“But I’m sure we all, as a family, community, will make sure if we have to do that, that will happen. But hopefully, as a baseline, we can go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. That would be really good.”

Audi team principal Mattia Binotto shares the same view and confirms that F1 teams should normally be informed by F1 around mid-October.

Mattia Binotto, Audi F1 Team Photo by: Joe Portlock / LAT Images via Getty Images

“As we discussed during the F1 Commission last Monday, mid-October is the last call for such a decision.”

Binotto does not see the potentially low temperatures as an obstacle to a possible season finale in Imola.

“The main challenges are more organisation and logistics, I would think. From a technical point, often we may say wintertime, snow tyres, but at the end, as a matter of fact, the average temperature in Imola in that time of the year is hotter than Las Vegas by the time we’ve got the race in Las Vegas.

“So I don’t think that’s a true concern. It’s more from the organisation and the logistics, really. And again, mid-October, hopefully we may do the right decision.”

Sports.title: Verstappen says engine problem cost him half a second to Hadjar | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen revealed a problem with his power unit left him at a disadvantage in qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver was quickest in the final practice session at the Baku City Circuit . However he fell to eighth in qualifying, four places behind his team mate Isack Hadjar

Verstappen’s final qualifying run was spoiled when Lando Norris went off in front of him, triggering yellow flags. But Verstappen said that was only “the last thing that happened” in a qualifying session which had already gone badly wrong.

“The whole qualifying, I’m just lacking top speed,” he told Sky. “I’m half a second a lap off just on top speed, even compared to my team mate. The engine was just not working. So that’s one problem.

“Then in Q3, in my middle lap, just trying to start the lap, the battery didn’t charge. So you start a lap with half a battery, so you have to abort, then you lose temperature because you don’t have enough power, basically. And that then snowballs into the final lap.

“I started the lap, but again, no top speed, a yellow flag in my lap, not enough tyre temperature, and then that’s where you are.”

Verstappen was second-fastest in Q1 and Q2 but he was slower in Q3 than in both the earlier sessions. “We were in a really good place the whole weekend and we had a disaster of a qualifying because of a lot of issues,” he concluded.

Sports.title: Sainz hit with grid drop and penalty points for second yellow flag infringement in Baku | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr has lost his best grid position of the season to date after being penalised for his second yellow flag infringement of the day in Baku.

The Williams driver avoided a grid drop for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags in final practice. However stewards hit him with a five-place grid drop when he repeated the offence in qualifying and added two penalty points to his licence, putting him on a total of four.

Sainz was reprimanded for his infringement in qualifying as the stewards ruled the yellow flag only appeared briefly during his lap. However Sainz passed multiple yellow flags during Q3 and failed to slow sufficiently.

Stewards’ verdict on Sainz’s final practice infringement

The stewards did not issue a grid drop to Sainz over his infringement in practice after taking into account how briefly the yellow flag was displayed for.

“A single yellow was displayed in marshalling sector six shortly before [Sainz] entered the sector,” the stewards ruled. “Sainz explained that, approaching turn four, he briefly noticed a light signal in his peripheral vision but was not certain that it was yellow. He therefore asked the team by radio whether a yellow flag was being displayed.

“The onboard video also showed that a yellow warning light was flashing on Sainz’s steering wheel, indicating the yellow sector. Sainz explained that in the circumstances he had not been able to pay attention to this warning.

“Approaching turn four, Sainz braked slightly earlier than on the reference lap, but subsequently applied less brake pressure. At the exit of turn four he accelerated more moderately than on the reference lap. Overall, he lost approximately 0.10 seconds in the relevant sector.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“From the exit of turn four Sainz was able to see the green light marking the end of the yellow sector. Sainz acknowledged that, having seen the green light, he should have understood that he was still travelling within a yellow sector. Nevertheless, on the straight approaching the green light he accelerated up to the limiter while still within the yellow sector.

“The stewards considered the fact that the single yellow was displayed only shortly before Sainz entered marshalling sector six as a mitigating circumstance. However, taking into account the visible yellow indication, the warning displayed on the steering wheel, the telemetry and, in particular, Sainz’s acceleration while still within the yellow sector after the green light had become visible, the stewards were not satisfied that Sainz had sufficiently reduced speed and exercised the required caution for a single yellow.

“The stewards therefore determine that Sainz failed to sufficiently reduce speed under the single yellow.

“The standard penalty under the Penalty Guidelines for such an infringement is a drop of five grid positions. However, the stewards considered that there were mitigating circumstances, in particular the very short period between the single yellow being displayed and Sainz entering the relevant marshalling sector. The stewards also considered the penalties applied in comparable cases, where a driving reprimand has consistently been imposed in circumstances warranting mitigation from the standard penalty. The stewards therefore considered a driving reprimand appropriate and consistent with those precedents.”

Stewards’ verdict on Sainz’s qualifying infringement

The stewards did not accept Sainz’s explanation for his second infringement.

“Single yellow flags were displayed in marshalling sectors four and five, in particular after turn two and on the approach to turn thee,” they noted. “The Yellow indications were clearly visible and Sainz had also received a radio warning from the team: “Yellow ahead, lift.” Sainz confirmed at the hearing that he was aware of the yellow Flag situation.

“SAI explained that he intended to demonstrate a reduction in speed across the yellow area as a whole. He stated that he did not consider it necessary to reduce speed on the straight and instead intended to demonstrate his response when approaching and exiting turn three. He considered this to be a “global lift” covering the consecutive Yellow sectors. He further explained that the car which had originally caused the yellow was no longer in the run-off area and that he expected the yellow flags to be withdrawn.

“The stewards did not accept this interpretation. Where consecutive marshalling sectors are subject to yellow flag conditions, a driver must demonstrate a significant reaction to reduce speed in each individual yellow marshalling sector. A reduction in a subsequent sector cannot retrospectively satisfy the requirement applicable to the preceding Yellow sector. The obligation is also not dependent on the driver’s own assessment of whether the original hazard remains present within a particular part of the Yellow sector.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The telemetry clearly showed that Sainz’s reaction to the Yellow occurred only in Marshalling Sector 5. There was no meaningful reduction in speed in marshalling sector four which could realistically be attributed to a response to the Yellow. Indeed, Sainz recorded his fastest time of the session in marshalling sector four.

“The stewards therefore did not accept that the subsequent lift in marshalling sector five constituted a sufficient “global” response covering both sectors. This is distinguishable from cases where the telemetry demonstrates a significant response to the Yellow even though the overall sector time reduction is relatively small. In the present case, Sainz was aware of the Yellow, had received an explicit warning from the team, the yellow indications were clearly visible and the telemetry established that he did not demonstrate the required reaction in marshalling sector four.

“The stewards therefore determine that Sainz failed to sufficiently reduce speed under the Single Yellow Flag in marshalling sector four.

“The standard penalty under the Penalty Guidelines for this infringement during qualifying is a drop of five grid positions.”

Sports.title: Antonelli “very mad” with himself after crashing out in first round of qualifying | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was frustrated with himself after crashing out of qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The championship leader hit the wall at the inside of turn one during Q1. He tried to drive his car back to the pits but his race engineer Peter Bonnington told him to stop as the suspension damage was too extensive for them to repair during the session.

Speaking after the session Antonelli said he was caught out by how quickly the grip levels increased at the track during the session.

“The grip was coming up very quickly lap-by-lap,” he told Sky. “Obviously I turned in and suddenly I had a lot more front-end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall.

“So it was mistake from my side. Very unnecessary, to be fair. I’m very mad about it and we’ll try to do better tomorrow.”

Antonelli missed a significant proportion of the first and second practice sessions yesterday due to a hydraulic problem. While Antonelli is set to start tomorrow’s race from 16th on the grid his team mate George Russell claimed pole position for the race.

“The car has been very strong this weekend, so George has been doing incredibly well,” said Antonelli. “We’ll try our best tomorrow to recover as many places as possible.”

Sports.title: Russell dominates Baku qualifying for pole after Antonelli crashes in Q1 | 2026 Azerbaijan GP qualifying report
Sports.content:
George Russell took pole position for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in dominant fashion.

His best lap of 1’42.526 was over eight tenths of a second quicker than anyone else could manage. He claimed pole position by the biggest margin for over three years

However his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli will start only 16th after he crashed out in the first round of qualifying.

The championship leader already had a time on the board when he clipped the barrier on the inside of turn one. The contact immediately broke his front-left suspension, and although Antonelli tried to drag his car back to the pits, race engineer Peter Bonnington persuaded him the suspension was so significant that the team wouldn’t be able to fix it in time and he should stop.

Compounding Antonelli’s misery, the time he had already set proved quick enough to secure him a place in Q2.

Russell’s bid for pole position briefly looked under threat from the McLaren drivers in Q3. However Lando Norris locked up heavily at turn three on his final lap and went into the run-off area. That also scuppered Max Verstappen’s final attempt to set a time, leaving him eighth on the grid.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Charles Leclerc produced his usual top-drawer performance at Baku to join Russell on the front row of the grid. Oscar Piastri, who set the quickest time at one stage in Q3, took third. Isack Hadjar out-qualified Verstappen on his return from injury.

Norris’s error left him fifth on the grid ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Both Alpine drivers reached Q3 but Franco Colapinto went off at turn 15 and ended up tenth, while Pierre Gasly took seventh ahead of Verstappen.

Carlos Sainz Jnr made good use of Williams’ upgrade, putting his car in Q3 for the first time this year. He will start ninth ahead of Colapinto.

Oliver Bearman narrowly failed to claim the final place in Q3 after Colapinto beat his time. Esteban Ocon also dropped out in Q2 in the other Haas. Alexander Albon was frustrated at his failure to join his team mate in the final 10 and dropped out along with the two Racing Bulls.

There was no great surprise that neither of the Aston Martins nor Cadillacs were able to beat Antonelli’s time in Q1. However the elimination of both Audis following their major upgrade was unexpected.

Sports.title: 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix grid | Formula 1
Sports.content: The Formula 1 world championship began in 1950 and is considered the world’s leading form of single-seater motorsport. The 2025 F1 season is the 75th time the championship has been held. [caption id="attachment_530322" align="alignright" width="470"] The 2025 Formula 1 season started in Australia[/caption]A world drivers’ champion has been crowned every year since the series began. Since 1958 a world constructors’ championship title has also been awarded. The most successful F1 drivers in history are seven-times world champions Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher. In 2021 the former became the first and so far only driver to date to win 100 grands prix. While Schumacher retired from F1 at the end of 2012, Hamilton continues to race. His rival world champions in the series are Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso. There are 10 teams active in the championship, each of which field cars for two drivers. Each team is required to design and build the majority of its cars but may source some parts including engines, gearboxes and certain other components. Ferrari has won the F1 constructors’ championship more times than any other team, with 16 titles. It is also the only team which has competed in every championship since the first…

Sports.title: Verstappen leads close final practice session in Baku ahead of Russell and Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of all three practice sessions for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

But there was little to choose between the three quickest teams at the end of the final hour of running before qualifying.

The Red Bull, Mercedes and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari were covered by little more than a tenth of a second.

Drivers found the soft tyres were capable of producing multiple quick laps. Verstappen improved his fastest time repeatedly over a 12-lap run on softs at the end of the session, but skidded into the turn 15 run-off area during his final attempt.

His last run nosed him ahead of Russell’s Mercedes, which had set the pace for much of the session. Russell and team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who was fourth-quickest, ducked back into the pits and switched to the medium compound before the session ended, while others continued to improve.

Charles Leclerc was half a second slower than Hamilton after going off at turn seven. Russell also came to a stop there during the session.

Pierre Gasly underlined Alpine’s potential again by setting the sixth-fastest time. That put him ahead of both McLaren drivers.

Sports.content:
Formula 1 could have one fewer race-winner on the grid in 2027 as Esteban Ocon has given the strongest indication yet he won’t remain at Haas.

Ocon is a mid driver at best. His race win in Hungary was not to do with skill and in a poor car, a mid driver cannot shine. The fact that Bearman is untroubled by Ocon’s ability is plain to see.

From a Haas perspective, keeping Ocon is a neutral equation. He’s not bringing in anything and having someone else in the car would make little to no difference to them from a sporting standpoint, it if having a Ferrari academy driver in the car gets them cheaper parts, why wouldn’t you?

Camara would be obvious for them given his current visibility across the F2 standings and the media. Couple that with his corporate backing and the fanaticism of Brazilian fans with wallets, he is a more attractive choice than a Mercedes journeyman with little in the way of an affiliation package.

Performance comes first, allegedly, but you can’t ignore financial performance. Besides, they’re not going to get Tsolov, Mini or Dunne so why not?

Sports.title: Fury vs. Benavidez? Coppinger’s Posts Turn Bizarre
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury against David Benavidez? Terence Crawford against Ryan Garcia as a replacement for Fury–Anthony Joshua? Two posts on Mike Coppinger’s X account floated those possibilities Friday, leaving boxing fans wondering what was going on with the account.

The first post claimed Fury–Joshua could fall apart and that Crawford–Ryan was under consideration as a replacement. A later post added Fury–Benavidez as “another possibility.” Neither matchup has been independently confirmed, and the posts alone are no basis for saying Fury–Joshua is off. The Ring had not publicly addressed the posts as of Friday evening.

The breakdown in the heavyweight negotiations comes straight from Coppinger on X:

“Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua could be called off due to issues, according to sources, and a replacement fight between Terence Crawford and Ryan Garcia is being considered. Another possibility: Tyson Fury-David Benavidez.”

Either Coppinger got his account compromised by a bored troll, or desperate promoters are feeding him unfiltered fantasy matchmaking straight out of a video game.

Floating Tyson Fury against David Benavidez is pure comedy. Benavidez only recently moved up to cruiserweight. Proposing that he jump straight past cruiserweight to share a ring with a 270-pound, six-foot-nine heavyweight is absurd on its face. It makes zero boxing sense, zero physical sense, and belongs in the bargain bin of panic-driven rumors.

What this really reveals is that the entire Cardiff December 11th date is in absolute freefall. When organizers go from trying to save Fury vs Joshua, to pitching Terence Crawford against Ryan at welterweight, to suddenly throwing Benavidez into the heavyweight division against Fury within minutes, you are watching outright chaos behind the scenes.

Someone inside those promotional rooms is throwing darts at a roster board hoping something sticks before the event disintegrates completely. Coppinger tweeting that nonsense out without laughing shows either total access-broker compliance or that somebody hijacked his phone in the press room.

The “issue” that is jeopardizing Fury-Joshua is Dana White’s involvement, multiple sources told @SInow. @Turki_alalshikh, who is bankrolling the fight, wants him as a promoter. AJ and Eddie Hearn don’t, and have a contract that says Zuffa can’t be. Fight very much in peril. — Chris Mannix (@SIChrisMannix) September 25, 2026

No contracts exist for a substitute bout, but the fact that organizers are entertaining Crawford against Ryan proves Fury vs Joshua is on life support. British promoters love dragging negotiations out until the entire event unravels. Cardiff fans booked hotels for a titanic domestic battle.

Ryan wiped out Conor Benn in two rounds, taking the WBC welterweight title at 147 pounds. Crawford retired last December after campaigning at super middleweight. Crawford walks around far bigger, carries superior technical skills, and possesses an iron chin.

Dragging Ryan into a ring against an elite fighter who campaigned at 168 pounds borders on malpractice. Turki Alalshikh has toyed with this idea, but paying both men enough to ignore the vast weight disparity will require exorbitant funds. Staging Crawford vs. Ryan inside a stadium in Wales makes zero promotional sense.

British ticket buyers bought into a decade of heavyweight drama. They have no interest in paying premium prices to watch two Americans settle an artificial catchweight experiment. Organizers need to stop floating absurd backup options and force their heavyweights to sign, or refund the public and pack up shop.

American boxing fans would jump at Terence Crawford vs Ryan over Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua any day of the week. Fury and Joshua have spent five years boring the public with broken promises, manufactured drama, and endless promotional theater. Stateside fans stopped caring about their stale domestic feud ages ago.

Dropping Crawford and Ryan into Cardiff never made a lick of sense. Welsh sports fans bought tickets to witness two British heavyweights collide in a stadium, not an all-American blockbuster flown across the Atlantic.

Packing that event up and shipping it directly to New York solves the entire problem overnight. Madison Square Garden or Barclays Center would sell out in minutes on December 11th. Ryan is the biggest draw in American boxing, fresh off demolishing Conor Benn in two rounds. Putting Ryan in the ring against Crawford in the fight capital of the world gives the US audience a massive pay-per-view spectacle in prime time.

New York athletic commissions know how to run giant events on short notice. Promoters would get full houses, high gate receipts, and ideal American broadcast hours instead of forcing US viewers to watch an afternoon heavyweight snoozer from the UK. If Fury and Joshua blow up their Cardiff date with their usual squabbling, bringing Crawford and Ryan to Manhattan is the only logical move.

Sports.title: Dana White Dares Eddie Hearn to Stop Him
Sports.content:
Dana White is already promoting Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua. That is his answer to Eddie Hearn’s claim that White cannot be involved in the December 11 fight in Cardiff.

Hearn says he will call Netflix about it. White has a simpler question: “Who’s going to stop me? Do you think Netflix give a [expletive] what Eddie Hearn thinks?” White said when asked about Hearn’s plan. “I guarantee they do not. I’m sitting here promoting the fight right now. Who’s going to stop me?”

White did not define his duties. He pointed to the event’s press release and said he was involved on Turki Alalshikh’s side, rather than with Fury or Joshua. Hearn may have a contractual objection to the scope of that role, but he has not laid one out publicly. The argument over White’s title has yet to prevent him from speaking about the event.

Matchroom built its name in an era when a promoter could control much of a major fight’s presentation. Fury–Joshua has a financier and a global broadcaster with interests of their own. Hearn represents a fighter the event needs, but that does not give him automatic control over everyone invited to help sell it. White’s arrival makes that change in power impossible to ignore.

Saying Netflix “didn’t get the memo” and promising to call the broadcaster looks especially weak when aired through interviews. If its press release conflicts with an agreement, Hearn has a serious issue to resolve directly. Telling the public he needs to correct Netflix first invites White to ask why the matter was not settled before the announcement. Netflix does not report to Matchroom, and those comments advertise a disagreement Hearn has yet to win.

There is a harder test of his influence. If keeping White out is essential, Hearn could tell the other parties that Joshua will not fight unless White is removed from the promotion. He has issued no such ultimatum. Fury–Joshua is a long-awaited fight with enormous money behind it, and threatening Joshua’s place on the card would be costly. Hearn has given no indication he is willing to make that move.

Joshua has not joined Hearn’s public objections in the exchanges at issue here. That does not tell us what Joshua thinks privately. It does leave his promoter carrying the complaint alone while White can argue that any attention he brings helps sell Joshua’s fight. The position would be stronger if the fighter whose participation gives Matchroom its influence made the same demand.

White also praised Fury promoter Frank Warren as a businessman with “less than zero ego,” then blamed “one whiny little crybaby” for the friction. The contrast is calculated. Warren is presented as willing to work within the arrangement; Hearn is cast as guarding his territory. White gets to define their roles each time the subject returns.

That may be Hearn’s most avoidable mistake. White thrives on an argument, and Hearn keeps supplying one. A dismissive sentence followed by a return to Joshua’s preparation would leave White to explain his own contribution. Instead, each complaint puts his name in another interview and gives him another clip to circulate. He becomes a co-star without having to finance the fight himself.

The dispute also travels beyond British boxing. White is familiar to American UFC viewers who may pay little attention to the usual exchanges between boxing promoters. A public fight with Hearn gives those audiences an easy way into the Fury–Joshua story. In trying to limit White’s presence, Hearn may be introducing him to the event’s wider audience.

Hearn may still secure limits on White’s role. Until he shows what he can enforce, though, White’s question hangs over every complaint: who is going to stop him?

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Invites Dana White Into Anthony Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says he removed a clause barring Dana White from his fight with Anthony Joshua. He says Joshua’s contract had the same restriction. Fury has made his choice public, leaving Joshua to answer an uncomfortable question: does he want White kept away from the event?

“I want him involved. Two baldies together,” Fury joked in an interview, as Dev Sahni reported. The contracts have not been made public, so Fury’s description of Joshua’s terms remains his account.

White’s involvement has already irritated Joshua’s promoter, Eddie Hearn. Fury knows that. His joke puts the issue in front of fans and invites them to see any objection from Joshua’s side as promoter politics getting in the way of a fight.

That is useful ground for Fury. If negotiations stall, he can say he welcomed everyone while Joshua’s side insisted on keeping White out. It gives Fury a simple explanation for a complicated delay, even though nobody has established that White’s role is what is holding up the fight.

It also puts Joshua in a difficult position. Matchroom helped make him a huge British attraction, and Hearn has every reason to protect his place in the promotion. But if Joshua wants White excluded too, fans deserve to hear that from Joshua. Fury’s version makes the restriction sound like Hearn guarding his territory.

There is another question Fury has left unanswered: what would White actually do? Neither boxer needs him to negotiate on his behalf. Wanting White “involved” sounds like a concession until someone defines the job Fury wants him to have.

Fury has found a line that will get people talking. A clear date, venue and agreement between both camps would do more for this fight than another argument over who gets a microphone.

Sports.title: Ricardo Sandoval Risks Two Titles Against Sergio Mendoza
Sports.content:
Ricardo Sandoval prepared for months to fight Oscar Collazo, a compact southpaw moving up to flyweight. With Collazo injured, Sandoval now has just over two weeks to adjust to Sergio Mendoza, a taller challenger with 23 knockouts who wants his WBA and WBC titles on October 10 in Chicago.

The change matters in the ring. Sandoval, listed at 5’6″, was preparing to face a much shorter fighter. Mendoza is listed at roughly 5’8″. The champion must adjust his distance and timing for an opponent who presents a different target and may make him work harder to get inside.

“I’m very excited to still be fighting in Chicago and to have the opportunity to defend my titles for the first time,” Sandoval said in the Golden Boy and Most Valuable Promotions announcement. Mendoza offered a more urgent message: “I’m going to leave my soul in the ring to become world champion.”

Sandoval (27-2, 18 KOs) has lost the unification fight that gave this date its appeal, yet he still has two belts to defend. Mendoza (27-1, 23 KOs) gets a second world title chance only months after Thanongsak Simsri stopped him in the second round of their April fight in Japan. That defeat raises a question about Mendoza’s ability to withstand the champion’s offense. It also gives him reason to seize this opportunity quickly.

Sandoval’s danger is fighting as though Mendoza is an obstacle between him and a rescheduled Collazo bout. If he rushes forward looking to make a statement, he gives a taller puncher chances to catch him coming in. A measured start would let Sandoval test Mendoza’s power and find the distance he did not spend camp preparing for.

Their flyweight title fight is the DAZN co-feature to Floyd Schofield III against Lucas Bahdi for the WBA lightweight title at Wintrust Arena.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Risks His Comeback Against Chev Clarke
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith has a chance to avenge two amateur losses to Chev Clarke on November 7. The danger is that Clarke’s best punches may come exactly where Billam-Smith likes to fight: up close.

Their 12-round cruiserweight bout will headline Zuffa Boxing 12 at London’s Copper Box Arena. Billam-Smith (22-2, 14 KOs) brings the world title experience. Clarke (12-2, 9 KOs) brings the amateur wins and the confidence of a fighter who has already beaten him twice.

Billam-Smith tends to make fights physical. He leans on opponents, works along the ropes and keeps punching when the exchanges get ugly. That served him in June against Ryan Rozicki, who did not come out for the eighth round after a punishing fight. Clarke’s win over Jack Massey on the same Bournemouth card showed a different kind of danger. Dropped twice in the fourth, Clarke recovered and stopped Massey in the seventh.

Billam-Smith cannot assume that crowding Clarke will make him safe. Clarke can fire short counters in those exchanges, and he showed against Massey that hurting him does not necessarily finish the job. But the knockdowns also give Billam-Smith an obvious target. If Massey could catch Clarke cleanly twice in one round, Billam-Smith has reason to test his chin early.

There is a question about what the Bournemouth fights took out of both men. Billam-Smith absorbed plenty from Rozicki; Clarke had to climb off the canvas twice. Neither gets a gentle return. For Billam-Smith, that comes after years of demanding cruiserweight fights and a world title loss to Gilberto Ramirez.

Clarke’s amateur edge gives this fight its history, but Billam-Smith has built the stronger professional career. He has won a world title and learned how to fight through difficult rounds. Clarke can change the direction of his career by beating him. Billam-Smith has far more to lose if a fighter he once struggled to beat stops his climb back toward another title shot.

Sky Sports will show the fight in the UK and Ireland; Paramount+ will stream it in the United States and Canada.

This fight is an elimination match between two aging cruiserweights running out of road. Clarke is thirty-five, entered the professional ranks late after the Tokyo Olympics, and has struggled to build real momentum toward the elite level. The two amateur wins over Billam-Smith happened a lifetime ago under a completely different scoring format.

In the professional ring, Clarke has looked vulnerable, particularly when Jack Massey put him on the canvas twice in June. Clarke survived because Massey got reckless, but banking on that kind of miraculous escape against top-tier punchers is suicide. A third professional loss buries Clarke on domestic undercards for the remainder of his days.

Billam-Smith is playing with fire by taking this fight. At thirty-six, his physical prime is fading fast. The beating he endured against Ryan Rozicki sent him directly to a hospital bed, proving that every victory now requires him to leave a piece of himself behind. He took heavy punishment from Gilberto Ramirez, endured a grueling scrap with Brandon Glanton, and took endless headshots from Rozicki.

Billam-Smith wanted Jai Opetaia, but settling for Clarke presents maximum risk with minimal reward. Losing to a domestic rival he is supposed to outwork destroys his credibility as a serious world title challenger. The stylistic matchup favors pure attrition over boxing finesse. Billam-Smith does not have the foot speed to keep Clarke on the outside, which guarantees a brutal battle in the pocket.

Clarke possesses power in the inside short spaces, which is precisely where Billam-Smith chooses to fight. If Clarke catches Billam-Smith clean early, the miles on Billam-Smith will show up instantly. Billam-Smith has the superior professional seasoning over twelve rounds. He knows how to drag opponents into deep waters, lean his weight on their shoulders, and grind them down along the ropes.

Sports.title: Johnny Fisher Weighs 243 Pounds for Michael Pirotton Fight at Zuffa Boxing 11
Sports.content:
Fisher headlines Saturday’s Copper Box Arena card, live on Paramount+ in the US and Sky Sports in the UK.

Johnny Fisher tipped the scales at 243 pounds ahead of his heavyweight clash with Michael Pirotton at London’s Copper Box Arena on Saturday, September 26. Belgium’s Pirotton weighed 240.6 pounds for their scheduled 10-round main event at Zuffa Boxing 11.

Fisher was 2.4 pounds heavier. Paramount+ will broadcast the event in the US, with Sky Sports carrying it in the UK. The event starts at 2 pm ET / 7 pm UK.

The Romford heavyweight enters at 14-1 with 12 knockouts after signing with Dana White’s promotion. Saturday will mark his third appearance at the Copper Box, where he also suffered his only professional defeat against Dave Allen.

Fisher had edged Allen by split decision in their first meeting before Allen stopped him in the rematch. He has since returned to winning ways, stopping Ivan Balaz in four rounds.

His move to Zuffa brings an immediate headline slot.

“The most exciting chapter of my professional career begins,” Fisher said when announcing his signing. “Thank you to Dana White, Nick Khan, and the Zuffa Boxing team for this opportunity. Everything has led to this point. Bull Army, get ready to assemble. Bosh!”

Richards and Kalajdzic Make Weight

Craig Richards registered 174.2 pounds for his 10-round light heavyweight bout against Radivoje Kalajdzic, who weighed 174.5 pounds. Both came in below the 175-pound limit.

Two middleweight bouts are scheduled for 10 rounds each. Lee Cutler weighed 159.5 pounds, with Louis Greene at 159.1, while Cesar Mateo Tapia hit 159.9 pounds against Leo Ruiz’s 159.2.

Kayla Allen and Edina Kiss will contest six rounds, weighing 142.9 pounds and 142 pounds, respectively. Alex MacMillan registered 149.9 pounds for his six-round meeting with Guillaume Azagier, who came in at 151.6.

Those bouts complete the six-fight main card.

Three Bouts on the Prelims

Rogelio Romero weighed 199.2 pounds ahead of his eight-round cruiserweight contest with Aurel Ignat, who registered 199.6 pounds.

Alexis de la Cerda and Cain Lewis both made the featherweight limit for their eight-rounder. De la Cerda came in at 125.4 pounds, with Lewis slightly heavier at 125.6.

Fred Pullen faces Leonardo Faretina over four rounds at lightweight. Pullen weighed 131.4 pounds, while Faretina registered 132.7, completing the nine-bout London bill.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Calls Shakur Stevenson’s Pacquiao Pursuit Easy Money
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley sees Shakur Stevenson’s pursuit of Manny Pacquiao as a soft move. With plenty of active fighters available, Shakur has picked a 47-year-old for the proposed co-feature on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua card.

“Ain’t nobody waiting on no damn Manny Pacquiao and you to fight, boy,” Bradley said in a video on his channel. He challenged Zuffa Boxing’s interest in the matchup, too: “Y’all talking about y’all supposed to be changing boxing? This ain’t changing boxing. This downplaying and downgrading boxing.”

Bradley first fought Pacquiao in 2012, when Manny was 33. Stevenson would face a far older fighter who has not recorded an official win since beating Keith Thurman in 2019. Putting Pacquiao’s name on Shakur’s record would be a commercial prize. It would say much less about Shakur’s place among today’s best fighters.

A Fury–Joshua stadium card would put Stevenson in front of viewers who rarely watch him. That opportunity comes with a trap. If he controls the distance and wins a quiet decision, a crowd waiting for Pacquiao’s old bursts of action may turn on him. If Shakur stops Pacquiao, many will see the result through the lens of Manny’s age. Winning the fight and winning over that audience are different jobs.

Stevenson also holds the WBO light welterweight title he took from Teofimo Lopez in January. Bradley pointed to Raymond Muratalla and O’Shaquie Foster while questioning why Shakur is pursuing Pacquiao. A catchweight attraction would take time away from a title defense, although the WBO has not approved this proposed fight or granted Stevenson an exception.

Bradley went further, claiming Floyd Mayweather wants Shakur to beat Pacquiao before Gervonta Davis gets the opportunity. That is Bradley’s speculation. His stronger point concerns Shakur’s own career: a famous opponent cannot give him the same credibility as beating a top fighter in his prime.

Pacquiao–Stevenson remains in talks for the proposed Fury–Joshua card in Cardiff. Bout agreements had not been delivered when the latest report was published.

Turki Alalshikh built his entire reputation among boxing purists on eliminating cherry-picks, forcing unifications, and making the fights the old promotional machinery spent a decade sabotaging. For Riyadh Season and Netflix to rubber-stamp an official, sanctioned bout between a prime pound-for-pound champion and an elderly senator looks like a total betrayal of that brand. It lowers the bar to YouTube celebrity boxing standards. Purists will openly question how the same organizers who put together elite 50-50 matchups can suddenly justify an exploitative nostalgia stunt on the biggest British stadium card of the year.

Turki Alalshikh built his entire reputation among boxing purists on eliminating cherry-picks, forcing unifications, and making the fights the old promotional machinery spent a decade sabotaging. For Riyadh Season and Netflix to rubber-stamp an official, sanctioned bout between a prime pound-for-pound champion and an elderly senator looks like a total betrayal of that brand. It lowers the bar to YouTube celebrity boxing standards. Purists will openly question how the same organizers who put together elite 50-50 matchups can suddenly justify an exploitative nostalgia stunt on the biggest British stadium card of the year.

Putting this fight as the co-feature in Cardiff sets a stylistic trap for everyone involved. Those stadium fans want blood, violence, and dramatic exchanges to warm them up for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Instead, they will watch Shakur do what he always does: use elite footwork, control distance from twenty feet away, and tap his way to a quiet, low-output decision against an icon whose forty-seven-year-old legs cannot track him down.

If Shakur refuses to engage and cruises to a boring points win, eighty thousand spectators will boo him mercilessly. If he turns aggressive and stops Pacquiao, fans will feel disgusted watching a faded legend get battered by someone nearly two decades younger. It produces a scenario where nobody wins, the sport loses credibility, and the fans leave feeling cheated by a spectacle disguised as competition.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Questions Hamzah Sheeraz’s Title Exit
Sports.content:
Frank Warren won the purse bid for Hamzah Sheeraz’s defense against Janibek Alimkhanuly. Days later, Sheeraz gave up the WBO super middleweight title. Warren’s response raises a question Sheeraz’s next fight will have to answer: what was the belt worth if he would not defend it against this challenger?

“Very, very disappointed,” Warren said in an interview this week. “It was a purse bid. We bid the highest amount of money for it.” Queensberry’s winning bid was $1,001,809, with Sheeraz due roughly $750,000 under the purse split. Warren said to iFL TV his team had worked to put Sheeraz in position to win the title.

Sheeraz mentioned Alimkhanuly’s previous failed drug test in objecting to the WBO’s order. He has grounds to question the sanctioning body’s decision. Still, surrendering the belt after Queensberry won the bid leaves him open to another question: what fight is worth giving up a guaranteed title defense?

Alimkhanuly would have been a serious test. Sheeraz had trouble controlling the mobile Simon Zachenhuber in July and kept his title by majority decision, with one judge scoring the fight level. Against Alimkhanuly, he would have faced a southpaw with greater power and a stronger claim to world class standing.

Warren also criticized the advice Sheeraz is receiving, then said Queensberry still has a contract with him. If Sheeraz is approaching his final fight under that deal and intends to leave, Warren has little incentive to arrange an easy farewell. A dangerous opponent would give Queensberry a fight to sell and give Sheeraz another chance to prove himself. Warren has announced no such plan, but his frustration makes the next matchmaking decision worth watching.

A champion brings a belt to the table when pursuing Canelo Alvarez or another major fight. Sheeraz no longer has that bargaining chip. If his team has a better opportunity ready, it can make the decision look shrewd. Until then, fans have seen him leave a difficult fight and a world title behind.

Fans never buy noble moral stances when a fighter surrenders a title to avoid an absolute nightmare. If Janibek were a feather-fisted fringe contender or an overmatched mandatory, Sheeraz walking away over money or a past testing issue might pass the smell test. When the mandatory opponent happens to be an avoided Kazakh wrecking ball with an elite amateur pedigree, the narrative completely crumbles.

Janibek represents the worst possible opponent profile in professional boxing: high risk, modest commercial value, and desperate hunger. He has been frozen out of massive unification bouts for years precisely because champions know the danger he brings. He saw Sheeraz holding that WBO belt as his golden ticket to finally force the sport to take him seriously and secure the life-changing purses he has been chasing. Facing a motivated, heavy-handed southpaw who knows his entire career trajectory hinges on dismantling you is a terrifying proposition.

Sheeraz clearly did the math and panicked. Taking Janibek for seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars offered terrible risk-to-reward math, especially after Simon Zachenhuber exposed how vulnerable Sheeraz looks when opponents start landing clean counters. Getting knocked out on home soil by Janibek permanently erases the mystique Queensberry spent years building.

The public sees right through the sudden ethical concerns. Turning down a dangerous fight against a prime killer while simultaneously campaigning to share the ring with Canelo Alvarez—who served a well-documented suspension for clenbuterol—makes the excuse look laughably dishonest. Sheeraz wanted the prestige of calling himself a world champion, but when the real tax for holding that strap arrived at the purse bid, he chose self-preservation over genuine greatness.

Ghana News.title: PKO trio eye victories at Odwira Festival
Ghana News.content:
Three PKO Boxing fighters are set to enter the ring at the Odwira Festival in Akropong, with all three having completed their weigh-in ahead of Saturday’s bouts.

Joseph “The Humble” Commodor will square off against Sani Yidana Kugblie, while Hamza Muhammad “Tank Hand” takes on John Oblitey Commey.

Juvenile boxer Rahman Lokko completes the PKO lineup and will face Benjamin Ankrah.

The fighters went through their weigh-in on Friday at the Attor Quarshie Gym in Jamestown, Accra, as preparations for the event reached the final stage.

Commodor comes into his fight with confidence after defeating Emmanuel Allotey by a fifth-round technical knockout.

Muhammad also has a victory behind him, having stopped Benya Bee in the first round at the Homowo Fight Night to register his first professional win.

Lokko, however, will be looking to return to winning ways after suffering a 2-1 points defeat against Prince Attor.

The PKO Boxing stable currently includes Africa Boxing League Light Heavyweight champion Prince Kamaldeen Mohammed, adding further championship experience to the outfit.

The PKO fighters will now look to translate their preparations into performances when they step into the ring in Akropong.

Ghana News.title: 346 Ghana Navy recruits pass out after 26 weeks of intensive training
Ghana News.content:
The Naval Recruit Training School (NRTS) of the Naval Training Command (NAVTRAC) has passed out 346 recruits of Basic Training Intake 85 (BT 85) following the successful completion of 26 weeks of military and basic naval training.

The passing out parade was held on Friday, September 25, at the NAVTRAC Parade Square at Nutekpor in the Volta Region.

The training combined classroom instruction, practical exercises and military drills designed to prepare the recruits for service in the Ghana Navy.

Speaking at the ceremony, the Volta Regional Minister, James Gunu, congratulated the recruits on completing the rigorous physical, academic and character training.

He reminded them that becoming members of the Ghana Armed Forces represented more than a change of uniform, but also the assumption of greater responsibility and the trust of the Ghanaian people.

Mr Gunu urged them to wear the military uniform with integrity, professionalism and patriotism, while discharging their duties with firmness, fairness, discipline and respect for human rights.

He further tasked the recruits to remain vigilant and professional in confronting emerging security threats, including armed robbery, land-guard activities, cybercrime, drug trafficking, substance abuse and threats to public order.

The Minister cautioned them against extortion, brutality and other forms of unprofessional conduct, urging them to become ambassadors of law and order.

He also commended the Commanding Officer and instructors for their efforts and assured the Armed Forces of the government's commitment to providing the logistics and resources required for training and operations.

Reviewing Officer urges discipline

The Reviewing Officer, Commodore Godson Kwabla Zowonoo (Rtd), also congratulated the recruits and urged them to uphold the values of loyalty, courage, integrity, discipline, professionalism, teamwork and selfless service instilled in them during their training.

He stressed that the passing out ceremony marked not the end of their development but the beginning of a lifelong journey of learning and professional growth.

Commodore Zowonoo encouraged the recruits to pursue continuous self-improvement, exercise sound judgement, respect lawful authority and remain committed to excellence.

He further reminded them that the naval uniform symbolises responsibility, trust and national service, and urged them to conduct themselves in ways that protect the reputation of the Ghana Navy and the wider Ghana Armed Forces.

He cautioned against corruption and abuse of authority, while encouraging the recruits to lead by example.

Outstanding recruits honoured

Several recruits received awards for outstanding performance during the training.

Recruit Petty Officer Class 1 Asafo-Agyei Audrey Kantanka was named Overall Best Recruit.

Recruit Chief Petty Officer Class 1 Alimenu Hamza received the Best in Drill award, while Ordinary Seaman Under Naval Training (OSUT) Amadi Blankson De-young Jnr was adjudged Best in Academics.

OSUT Sadiq Huseifa received the Commanding Officer’s Special Award.

The ceremony was attended by the South Tongu District Chief Executive, Victoria Dzeklu, former Chief of the Naval Staff Rear Admiral Geoffrey Mawuli Biekro (Rtd), senior officers, instructors, Senior Rates, as well as families and friends of the graduating recruits.

The Ghana Navy Regimental Band also provided ceremonial support.

Ghana News.title: Newsfile to discuss EOCO-MP arrest, drug trafficking, speech arrests and $235m water debt
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile, returns on Saturday, September 26, with host Samson Lardy Anyenini leading discussions on four major issues dominating Ghana’s national conversation.

EOCO chases MP: Immunity or impunity?

The first major discussion will focus on the reported confrontation involving Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah and the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO).

The programme will examine the circumstances surrounding the attempted arrest of the legislator and the wider constitutional questions surrounding parliamentary immunity, arrest procedures and the limits of law-enforcement powers.

The discussion will also consider whether parliamentary privileges protect MPs from arrest and how such privileges should be balanced against ongoing investigations.

Drug busts: Clergy alarm, MPs recalled – NACOC working?

Newsfile will also turn its attention to Ghana’s growing drug-trafficking concerns.

The discussion comes amid alarm over recent drug busts and calls for stronger action against narcotics trafficking. The panel will examine the role of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) and whether existing measures are sufficient to tackle the growing threat.

The programme will also consider the decision to recall MPs and the broader implications of recent developments for Ghana’s security and international reputation.

Speech arrests: JM preaches restraint – nurse still caged

Another key issue will be the growing debate over arrests linked to speech and online activity.

Newsfile will examine President John Dramani Mahama’s call for restraint in dealing with speech-related cases, alongside the continued detention of a nurse whose case has generated public discussion about freedom of expression and the enforcement of laws governing online content.

The panel will explore where the line should be drawn between unlawful speech and legitimate criticism, as well as the responsibilities of law-enforcement agencies in handling such cases.

$235m water debt: $126m plant, no water – fixing the mess

The final major topic will focus on the US$235 million water debt linked to the desalination plant.

The programme will examine how Ghana came to face the substantial liability despite the plant having reportedly cost about US$126 million, and why the facility is not currently delivering the expected water supply.

The panel will discuss the circumstances surrounding the project, the financial implications for the state and possible measures to address the situation.

Joining Samson Lardy Anyenini are:

Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah – Vice-Chair, Subsidiary Legislation Committee and member, Constitutional and Legal Affairs Committee of Parliament.

– Vice-Chair, Subsidiary Legislation Committee and member, Constitutional and Legal Affairs Committee of Parliament. Inusah Fuseini – Former MP for Tamale Central and former Minister for Lands and Natural Resources.

– Former MP for Tamale Central and former Minister for Lands and Natural Resources. Rev. John Ntim Fordjour – Ranking Member, Defence and Interior Committee and MP for Assin South.

– Ranking Member, Defence and Interior Committee and MP for Assin South. Alexander Twum-Barimah Esq. – Deputy Director-General, NACOC.

– Deputy Director-General, NACOC. Bobby Banson – Lawyer and lecturer, Ghana School of Law, Makola.

– Lawyer and lecturer, Ghana School of Law, Makola. Dr John Osae-Kwapong – Director, Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness, Ashesi University and an institute fellow with CDD-Ghana.

Ghana News.title: JoyNews gets results as listeners raise GH¢40,000 to help 17-year-old student with cerebral palsy attend SHS
Ghana News.content:
Seventeen-year-old Priscilla Nana Ama Samson, a student living with cerebral palsy, has returned to senior high school after Ghanaians rallied to support her education.

Priscilla had feared she would be unable to resume school because her mother could not afford the items listed on her school prospectus.

Her situation was highlighted by JoyNews, prompting an overwhelming response from listeners and members of the public.

About GH¢40,000 has since been raised to help Priscilla meet her school-related needs and return to the classroom.

With the support, Priscilla has now resumed school and joined her peers as she begins a new chapter of her education.

Her return marks a significant change from the uncertainty she faced when the cost of basic school requirements threatened to keep her at home.

The support has also provided relief for her mother, who had been struggling to meet the financial demands of sending her daughter back to school.

For Priscilla, however, the immediate worry of whether she would be able to return to school has been replaced by the opportunity to continue her education alongside her peers.

The family has expressed appreciation to the JoyNews audience and all those who contributed to making her return to school possible.

Ghana News.title: Vice President calls for stronger local pharmaceutical production to reduce medicine imports
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for stronger local pharmaceutical production as Ghana seeks to reduce its reliance on imported medicines and improve access to essential drugs.

She said expanding the capacity of Ghanaian pharmaceutical manufacturers would strengthen the health system and help the country respond more effectively to changing healthcare needs.

The Vice President was speaking in Accra at the opening of the 90th Anniversary Annual General Meeting and Scientific Conference of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana.

She noted that local manufacturers were already building capacity to produce a wider range of essential medicines and pharmaceutical products.

“Local manufacturers are developing capacity to produce infusions, injectables, ophthalmic products and anaesthetics,” she said.

Professor Opoku-Agyemang said increasing local production would not only strengthen the pharmaceutical industry but also improve access to essential medicines.

The government is pursuing a five-year strategy to increase the proportion of medicines manufactured locally from 30% to 70%.

Pharmaceutical Society calls for funding

President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana, Pharm. Paul Owusu Donkor, welcomed the 70% target but said achieving it would require sustained government support.

“We therefore ask the government of Ghana to turn its five-year strategy into a funded delivery program,” he said.

He called for predictable public procurement of quality-assured medicines manufactured in Ghana, timely payment of suppliers and access to affordable long-term financing for pharmaceutical manufacturers.

According to him, these measures would give local producers greater certainty to invest in production capacity and contribute to the government’s target.

Focus on changing health needs

Beyond pharmaceutical manufacturing, Professor Opoku-Agyemang urged pharmacists to play a greater role in addressing Ghana’s growing burden of chronic and non-communicable diseases.

She also called for regulation to keep pace with technological changes affecting healthcare, including artificial intelligence, digital prescribing and evolving medicine supply chains.

The Vice President said Ghana’s changing health needs require a health system capable of detecting diseases early, managing conditions effectively and preventing avoidable complications.

The conference is being held under the theme “Science. Impact. Legacy: 90 Years of Pharmaceutical Excellence.”

The 90th anniversary event is providing a platform for discussions on the future of Ghana’s pharmaceutical sector, access to medicines and measures to build greater resilience within the health system.

Ghana News.title: The brewing tension at KNUST; Beware the Ides of October….
Ghana News.content:
Less than a month after the investiture of a new Vice-Chancellor, the Governing Council of KNUST has decided to end a practice that has been part of KNUST's academic governance for generations: faculty will no longer elect their own Deans and Pro-Vice-Chancellors. They will be appointed.



The timing alone should make everyone pause. A new administration has barely settled in, and already one of the University's longest-standing traditions of academic participation is being dismantled. Even more troubling is that Council is proceeding despite formal petitions from the major recognized staff unions, UTAG, GAUA and TEWU-TUC, strongly opposing the change. These are not peripheral voices; they represent the staff whose participation in the governance of the University is now being removed.

It is therefore much bigger than a change in procedure; it is a transfer of power from the academic community to the centre.



From time immemorial, academics and senior administrators have had a say in choosing their academic leaders. The system may have had weaknesses, but it has also produced leaders who enjoyed the confidence of the academic community (Professors Rita Dickson, Otoo Ellis, Adarkwa, and Odai are examples). If there are problems with the elections, fix them, tighten the rules, and improve the safeguards while making the process more transparent. But don't abolish participation because it is difficult to manage.



There is also a democratic irony that should not be lost on us. In Ghana today, ‘even’ a head porter has the constitutional right to participate in choosing the President of the Republic. Yet at KNUST, academics and senior administrators (the people who teach, research, supervise students and run the academic enterprise) are being denied the opportunity to participate in choosing those who lead their academic units.

Today it is Deans and ProVCs; tomorrow, what other forms of participation might be considered unnecessary or inconvenient?



October 2018 should still be fresh in our minds; a disagreement at KNUST escalated into a major institutional crisis, leading to disruption, destruction of property, closure of the University and dissolution of the Governing Council. We should be doing everything possible to ensure that history does not repeat itself.



Council has the authority to make decisions, yes. But having the authority to do something does not necessarily make every decision you take right. Good governance is not simply about the power to decide; it is also about knowing when to listen, when to consult, and when to reconsider.



And let us be clear: this is not merely about who becomes Dean or ProVC; it is about what kind of KNUST we want. A University that teaches critical thinking cannot afford to become intolerant of critical voices within its own walls.



KNUST has only recently restored its academic calendar after considerable disruption. The last thing the University needs is another avoidable confrontation. If this dispute escalates, students, lecturers, researchers and ultimately the University's reputation will suffer.



We have been here before. KNUST does not need another October 2018. It needs dialogue, consultation and statesmanship now. Council should pause and engage the unions seriously. Because once you take away a community's voice, you cannot simply expect its trust to remain intact.

Ghana News.title: Health Ministry moves to integrate traditional medicine into mainstream healthcare
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Minister for Health, Prof. Dr Grace Ayensu-Danquah, has called for greater integration of scientifically validated traditional medicine into Ghana’s mainstream healthcare system.

She said traditional medicine, when properly researched, regulated and manufactured to approved standards, could play a significant role in expanding access to safe and quality healthcare.

Prof. Ayensu-Danquah made the call when she visited the Centre of Awareness (COA) Research and Manufacturing Company in the Central Region, where she engaged management and staff and inspected the company’s facilities to assess its compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).

She said Ghana could learn from countries such as China, where traditional and conventional medicine are used alongside each other to complement healthcare delivery.

According to her, closer collaboration between the two sectors could help improve healthcare outcomes while ensuring that traditional medicines used by the public meet the required standards for safety, quality and effectiveness.

Prof. Ayensu-Danquah said the government’s Free Primary Healthcare programme, which places emphasis on preventive and promotive healthcare, also presented an opportunity to examine how traditional medicine could contribute to the delivery of primary healthcare.

She identified non-communicable diseases, including hypertension and diabetes, as areas where traditional medicine could potentially contribute, subject to scientific validation and appropriate regulation.

The CEO of COA Manufacturing Company, Prof. (HC) Samuel Ato Duncan, welcomed the government’s efforts to develop the traditional medicine sector to a standard that would enable it to complement national healthcare programmes, including the Free Primary Healthcare initiative.

He said the company was undertaking research into the potential health benefits of some of its products, including their possible applications in the management of cancer and viral diseases.

Prof. Duncan stressed the importance of continued research and collaboration between traditional medicine practitioners, researchers and government institutions in unlocking the potential of the sector.

He said such collaboration could help strengthen the evidence base for traditional medicines and enable the sector to make a greater contribution to healthcare delivery in Ghana.

Prof. Ayensu-Danquah said the Ministry of Health would continue to work with relevant stakeholders to strengthen research, quality assurance, manufacturing and regulation within the traditional medicine sector.

She said the broader objective was to create a healthcare system in which traditional and conventional medicine could complement each other safely, based on scientific evidence and appropriate regulatory standards.

Ghana News.title: 550 pupils in Kintampo South get educational lifeline as ‘Seeds of Hope’ reaches farming communities
Ghana News.content:
More than 550 pupils in two farming communities in the Kintampo South District have received school supplies as part of an outreach programme aimed at easing some of the educational challenges confronting children in rural Ghana.

The intervention formed part of the 2026 “Seeds of Hope” Community Outreach and School Donation Campaign by SeedSpark Foundation, in partnership with Legacy Impact through the Legacy Career Institute and OhenebaCare Foundation.

The school gates in Anokyekrom and Abom Komkomba had barely opened on Monday, September 21, 2026, when the communities began buzzing with activity.

Volunteers were setting up, health workers were preparing for free screening, and boxes of books and other educational materials were being arranged for pupils.

For the children, however, the excitement was about more than a change from the usual school routine.

They were about to receive some of the basic items many of them need to participate fully in the classroom.

A total of 250 pupils in Anokyekrom and 300 in Abom Komkomba, from Kindergarten through Junior High School, received exercise books, textbooks, pens, pencils, rulers, school bags, clothing and footballs.

The schools also received textbooks and Teaching and Learning Materials for use by teachers.

For some teachers, the donation addresses a challenge that is familiar in many rural classrooms — trying to deliver lessons with limited teaching and learning resources.

A teacher at Abom Komkomba D/A School welcomed the intervention, saying the textbooks would support both teachers and pupils.

“The textbooks we’ve received will help us study and teach the kids,” she said.

She added that some pupils regularly report to school without exercise books, making the donation particularly important.

“This will help them and make learning and teaching enjoyable and easier. God bless SeedSpark Foundation,” she said.

Executive Director of SeedSpark Foundation, Henry Ekow Yawson, said the organisation deliberately focuses on farming communities, where children can sometimes have fewer educational resources despite their communities playing an important role in Ghana’s food production.

“Communities like Anokyekrom and Abom Komkomba are the backbone of this country’s food supply, yet their children are often the last to receive the tools they need to learn,” he said.

According to him, the Foundation intends to continue returning to such communities because educational opportunity should not depend on where a child is born.

“Every child deserves a fair shot, no matter where they’re born,” he added.

The organisers say the intervention was designed to go beyond a one-day distribution exercise.

Director of Legacy Impact, David, spoke to the pupils about opportunities available through the Legacy Career Institute and encouraged them to remain committed to their education.

He said the objective was to help the children understand that their current circumstances do not have to define the limits of their future.

“We don’t just want to hand out books and leave. We want these children to know that there’s a path beyond this classroom,” he said.

Volunteers also spent time with the pupils, engaging them through games, singing and conversations.

For the organisers, those interactions were just as important as the physical donations because they created an opportunity to encourage the children directly.

The outreach also brought healthcare services closer to residents.

An 18-member medical team comprising personnel from Kintampo South Hospital, OhenebaCare Foundation and the National Health Insurance Scheme screened an estimated 160 residents.

The NHIS component was particularly targeted at helping residents understand and access the scheme while ensuring farmers who needed registration or renewal support could receive it during the outreach.

Organisers plan to expand the campaign to more communities and undertake follow-up visits.

Those visits are expected to help identify and respond to some of the needs uncovered during the education and health activities.

By the end of the day, the classrooms at Anokyekrom and Abom Komkomba had gained new teaching materials, hundreds of pupils had received school supplies and dozens of residents had accessed health services.

But for SeedSpark Foundation and its partners, the campaign represents something broader than a single day’s activities.

It is an attempt to put practical resources behind a simple proposition: that a child’s access to education should not be determined by whether they grow up in a farming community or a major urban centre.

The Foundation says the work will continue under its guiding motto: “Seeds of Change, Sprout of Success.”

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
