World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: KRA seizes 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret Airport
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The consignment was intercepted by KRA enforcement teams following an intelligence report.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has seized a consignment containing 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret International Airport, averting a potential tax loss of Sh21.5 million.

KRA enforcement teams intercepted the consignment after an intelligence report indicated it contained undeclared mobile phones and other high-end electronic goods.

The cargo, which had been declared under five Customs entries, was part of consolidated shipments that also included shoes, clothing, automotive spare parts, household goods, electronic accessories and other assorted items.

KRA said an initial declaration listed only 3,000 smartphones. However, verification established 55,607 ordinary smartphones, alongside 309 undeclared high-end smartphones.

The high-end devices included Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max models.

“The consignment therefore reflects both under-declaration and non-declaration of dutiable goods,” KRA said in a statement issued on Wednesday.

The tax authority said the verification exercise was conducted to establish whether all mobile phones contained in the consignment had been properly declared.

KRA said the alleged tax evasion contravenes Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), 2004.

The law provides that a person who makes a false or incorrect Customs entry, or knowingly participates in the fraudulent evasion of duty, commits an offence.

“A person who, in any matter relating to Customs, makes any entry which is false or incorrect in any particular, or in any way is knowingly concerned in any fraudulent evasion of the payment of any duty, commits an offence,” KRA said, citing the law.

According to the authority, a person convicted under the provision is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a fine of up to US$10,000.

KRA said it was intensifying efforts to uncover tax evasion schemes to improve revenue compliance and ensure adherence to tax laws and procedures.

“KRA is actively engaged in unearthing tax evasion schemes to boost tax revenue compliance as well as adherence to tax laws and procedures, hence ensuring fair trade is maintained within the market,” the authority said.

The authority also appealed to members of the public, taxpayers and businesses with information on individuals, companies or networks involved in the generation, sale, purchase or use of fictitious VAT invoices to report them.

KRA said information provided would be treated confidentially and the identity of informants kept anonymous.

World.title: 'We know what happened': Uhuru claims Raila won 2022 polls
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [File, Standard]

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta says he remains convinced that Raila Odinga won the 2022 presidential election.

Speaking during a Jubilee Party meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, September 22, Uhuru questioned how the Azimio coalition could have lost the presidency despite performing strongly in other elective races.

“We did everything to help Baba become President of the Republic of Kenya. He got the votes, and to this day I know that he is the one who won those votes. We know how things happened, and we do not want it to happen that way again,” Uhuru said.

The late Odinga contested the August 9, 2022 election under the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition Party, with Martha Karua as his running mate. Ruto ran under the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as the presidential candidate of the Kenya Kwanza Alliance.

Ruto was declared president-elect after garnering 7,176,141 votes, 50.49 per cent, against Odinga's 6,942,930 votes, 48.85 per cent. Ruto's margin was 233,211 votes.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld his election after dismissing petitions challenging the results.

But Uhuru pointed to the coalition's performance in the parliamentary and county races to question how Azimio could have lost the presidency.

“How can you say we were defeated when we had most of the MPs, governors and senators? How were we defeated in the presidency?” he asked.

In the National Assembly, figures published after the election initially put Azimio ahead of Kenya Kwanza, with 165 seats against 160, while 12 seats were held by independent MPs.

Azimio also won 23 of the 47 governorships, while Kenya Kwanza secured 22. The remaining two were won by Taita Taveta Governor Andrew Mwadime and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, who ran as independent candidates.

In the Senate, Kenya Kwanza had an advantage, winning 24 of the 47 directly elected seats against Azimio's 23.

The parliamentary balance later shifted in favour of Kenya Kwanza after several MPs changed their political allegiance.

In October 2022, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula declared Kenya Kwanza the majority coalition with 179 MPs against Azimio's 157, after several MPs from parties including UDM, MDG, Maendeleo Chap Chap and PAA moved towards the Kenya Kwanza side.

Uhuru also rejected claims that he was responsible for Odinga's loss, saying he was not a candidate in the election.

“I am surprised when people say that we did not help Baba and that they defeated me. I was not on the ballot, and they are lying. I was only Raila's handyman,” he said.

He warned against what he described as divisive and dirty politics, saying Kenya should not repeat the events surrounding the 2022 election.

“Dirty politics and politics aimed at dividing Kenyans will take us nowhere. Let us not divide each other. What does it help us? Sell your manifesto,” Uhuru said.

He said he accepted the Supreme Court's decision after the 2022 presidential petitions and handed over power to Ruto without disputing the outcome, accusing Ruto of dragging his name in his failed leadership.

“When we finished and the court ruled, we did not dispute it. We went and handed over the presidency to them. And now, after four years, they are still talking about Uhuru. But when things are not working, people tend to look for excuses,” he said.

This is the clearest public assertion by the former president since the 2022 elections that Odinga won the presidential vote.

World.title: Ruto offers Kenya as test case on African risk
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto with Dangote Industries President and CEO Aliko Dangote and Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) CEO Samaila Zubairu on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

President William Ruto has offered Kenya as a test case for how African risk is assessed, saying the country will open its default and recovery data to rating agencies and accept changes to the methodology if the evidence supports them.

Ruto said financial rules are steering African pension savings towards government securities rather than infrastructure, even where regulations allow greater investment in projects.

He made the proposal Monday, September 21, at the Africa We Build High-Level Roundtable on regulation, risk and reward in New York. The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) convened the event on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Kenyan pension funds hold 46 per cent of their Sh3.2 trillion ($24.7 billion) in government securities but only 0.02 per cent in infrastructure debt, Ruto said. The rules allow pension funds to invest up to 10 per cent in infrastructure.

“Africa's problem is no longer the amount of capital available to it. Africa's problem is the set of rules that decide where that capital is allowed to go,” Ruto noted.

Ruto returned to an argument he made at the inaugural Africa We Build Summit in Nairobi in April, where he said African countries should use domestic capital to finance their own infrastructure.

At the New York roundtable, he revisited his earlier phrase, “he who pays the piper calls the tune”, using a teacher in Eldoret who has contributed to a pension fund for 20 years to illustrate his point.

“In Nairobi I said that he who pays the piper calls the tune. I meant it as a warning about depending on other people's money. This morning I mean it as an opportunity. The teacher in Eldoret is paying the piper. She has earned the right to call the tune,” Ruto explained.

He said the teacher's savings are more likely to sit in a US Treasury bill than in a nearby geothermal plant.

“Her fund manager is not being unpatriotic. He is being rational. The rules he works under tell him the Treasury bill is prudent and the power plant is adventurous. Capital follows incentives, and we wrote the incentives,” Ruto observed.

The Africa Finance Corporation's President and Chief Executive Samaila Zubairu framed the wider problem in similar terms at the Nairobi summit, saying Africa is “not capital-poor; it is capital-trapped.”

Ruto now wants African risk assessed using evidence from African markets rather than assumptions that he argues can make projects and countries appear more expensive to finance.

He said Kenya will make its pension and insurance regulators available to work with rating agencies, insurers and standard setters.

“If the evidence vindicates the current methodology, we will accept the finding and say so publicly. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto added.

He proposed that the roundtable establish a working group based in Nairobi to continue the work and report to the next Africa We Build Summit in 12 months with findings backed by numbers.

President William Ruto on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

Ruto made four requests to rating agencies, insurers, regulators and other institutions involved in financing: price African risk against African experience, make insurance on productive assets affordable, end penalties on long-term assets in prudential and liquidity rules and build bankable project pipelines.

He said African non-bank domestic capital pools have passed $2 trillion, while external concessional and commercial flows to Africa totalled $1.7 trillion between 2014 and 2024.

Official development assistance has also fallen every year since 2020, Ruto said, arguing that Africa can no longer rely on external financing to meet its infrastructure needs.

Kenya has begun putting some of the proposed financing mechanisms in place.

Ruto said the National Infrastructure Fund, signed into law in March, aims to mobilise up to $40 billion for roads, ports, power and water without new public debt.

In May, Kenya listed its first infrastructure fund on the Nairobi Securities Exchange and raised Sh3.4 billion with United Kingdom support. Kenya also increased its equity in the Africa Finance Corporation by Sh3.25 billion ($25 million), Ruto said.

The president said Kenya was willing to expose its own financing system to scrutiny as part of the test.

“If the evidence supports the current methodology, we will accept it. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto told the roundtable.

The broader goal, he said, is to make it as easy for African institutional investors to finance productive assets as it is to buy government debt.

“The day a Kenyan pension trustee can buy a Kenyan power station as easily as she buys a Treasury bill, this argument will be over,” Ruto said.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro, Kinangop MP clash over alleged threatening message
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro arrives at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town for the service on September 20, 2026. [James Munyeki, Standard]

There was drama at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town during service on Sunday after Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro clashed with Kinangop MP Zachary Kwenya Thuku over an alleged threatening message.

Thuku, who is allied to the Kenya Kwanza government led by President William Ruto, is said to have warned Nyoro against attending the service.

"Yesterday, I received a message from the MP for Kinangop, Kwenya Thuku, warning me not to attend the church service. If I am lying, let him come here and read the message he sent me," Nyoro said.

He challenged the Kinangop MP to read the message aloud to the congregation.

"If anything happens to me today, Kenyans will judge whoever will be responsible," said Nyoro.

The Kiharu MP challenged Thuku to face him at a public rally at Engineer Trading Centre.

When he rose to speak, the Kinangop MP said he would not address the matter in church.

Instead, he said this was a political issue that the leaders would resolve.

"Let us solve this matter amicably. We are all brothers in this political journey," he said amid cheers from the congregation.

Recently, Nyoro added his voice to the growing political realignment in Mt Kenya, openly acknowledging the political tightrope he now walks as he distances himself from his former allies in the ruling party.

In a candid interview, he admitted that his previous close ties with President William Ruto and the Kenya Kwanza administration have left him vulnerable to suspicion from both sides of the political divide but insisted his decision to abandon the ruling party, United Democratic Alliance (UDA) was deliberate, difficult, and necessary.

World.title: Ruto leaves for New York ahead of UN General Assembly
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto leaves for New York ahead of 81st UN General Assembly. [PCS]

President William Ruto has departed for New York, United States, to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Ruto is expected to push Kenya’s investment agenda and advocate for increased financing for Africa.

According to a statement from State House, Ruto will use the global gathering to seek partnerships in energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, health, agriculture and technology.

He will also advance Kenya’s agenda on artificial intelligence and Africa’s participation in the global digital economy.

Ruto is expected to co-chair roundtables hosted by the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Global Africa Business Initiative (GABI), alongside industrialist Aliko Dangote.

A key focus will be the planned Sh2.2 trillion East Africa Refinery in Lamu, which the government says will have a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and create more than 60,000 jobs. The project is scheduled to break ground on September 30, 2026.

On artificial intelligence, Ruto and Finland President Alexander Stubb will co-lead the AI Middle Powers Initiative, which seeks to enable countries to pool computing resources, data and talent to build AI capabilities.

Kenya will also advance the Africa Development Bank-backed AI 10 billion initiative, which aims to mobilise up to 10 billion dollars by 2035 for investment in Africa’s artificial intelligence sector.

The President is further expected to sign a global declaration and roadmap on child online AI safety alongside leaders from Spain, the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.

He will also launch an Africa Resilience Compact that will use artificial intelligence, satellite earth observation and predictive technologies to strengthen preparedness for El Niño and other climate shocks.

During his address to the UN General Assembly, Ruto is expected to champion an Africa-financing-Africa approach, calling for reforms and international guarantees to unlock more African capital for infrastructure and enterprise.

Ruto will also highlight Kenya’s National Infrastructure Fund, which the government says is designed to mobilise up to 40 billion dollars without adding to public debt.

On the sidelines of the General Assembly, the President is expected to hold meetings with heads of state and government, multilateral institutions and global corporations to discuss trade, investment and diplomatic cooperation.

He will also engage Kenyans living in the United States as the government advances a Diaspora Investment Platform intended to channel diaspora capital into productive investment in Kenya.

World.title: New winter closing hours take effect for shops and restaurants starting Friday
World.content:
Winter operating hours for various commercial activities take effect on Friday, September 25.

Under the new schedule, commercial shops and shopping malls will open daily at 7:00 AM and close at 10:00 PM, with closing times extended until 11:00 PM on Thursdays, Fridays, and official national holidays.

Restaurants, cafés, and bazaars will begin operations at 5:00 AM and close at midnight daily, with operating hours extended until 1:00 AM on Thursdays, Fridays, and public holidays. Takeaway and 24-hour home delivery services will continue without interruption.

Exempted activities and seasonal schedule transition

In addition, workshops and craft businesses located within residential areas are permitted to operate daily from 8:00 AM until 6:00 PM. Exceptions are granted to workshops situated along highways or affiliated with service stations, which are governed by specific operational directives issued by local administration authorities.

The decree excludes critical services to ensure continuous public convenience. Exempted establishments include grocery stores, supermarkets, bakeries, and pharmacies, alongside fruit, vegetable, poultry, and meat markets.

The implementation of winter business hours operates independently of daylight saving time adjustments. Standard winter time will officially resume on the final Thursday of October—October 29—when clocks will be turned back 60 minutes at midnight to become 11:00 PM.

World.title: Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro reunite as ‘Focker-In-Law’ sets late November premiere in Egyptian and North American theaters
World.content:
The long-running comedic feud between the Focker and Byrnes clans is officially reigniting as Universal Pictures prepares to roll out “Focker-In-Law”, the next chapter in the hit “Meet the Parents” franchise. The film is slated to debut across North American cinemas on November 25, followed immediately by its Egyptian theatrical release on November 26.

Arriving more than a decade after 2010’s “Little Fockers”, the PG-13 comedy sees Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro step back into their iconic roles as the perpetually anxious Greg Focker and his stern, ex-CIA father-in-law Jack Byrnes.

A new generation takes center stage

This latest entry shifts the comedic spotlight onto Greg and Pam’s now-grown son, Henry Focker (Skyler Gisondo). The family dynamic hits a fresh wall of chaos when Henry decides to settle down with Olivia Jones, played by franchise newcomer Ariana Grande.

Olivia, a former FBI hostage negotiator, brings her own high-stakes family baggage to the table. As wedding bells approach, the clash between the two households sparks a fresh series of covert suspicions, awkward misunderstandings, and classic Focker mayhem—placing Greg in the unfamiliar position of playing mediator between the old guard and the new generation.

Ensemble cast and creative team

Alongside Stiller, De Niro, Gisondo, and Grande, the film brings back beloved franchise veterans including Owen Wilson, Blythe Danner, and Teri Polo, while introducing new additions Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco.

Director John Hamburg, who co-wrote the original three “Meet the Parents” installments, returns to steer the franchise as both writer and director. Hamburg developed the screenplay from a story co-crafted with Ilana Glazer and Austen Earl. The production team brings together industry heavyweights, with Jane Rosenthal, Robert De Niro, Ben Stiller, John Lesher, Jay Roach, and John Hamburg serving as producers.

World.title: Gaza Strip facing the world’s worst economic crisis: UN report
World.content:
The United Nations has issued a stark warning regarding the Gaza Strip, declaring that the enclave is now gripped by the most severe economic breakdown anywhere on the planet. Ongoing military conflict has effectively dismantled local commerce, erased key infrastructure, and stripped nearly two million residents of their basic livelihoods.

A newly released assessment by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) paints a grim picture of the territory’s financial health, revealing that total economic output in Gaza has plummeted by a staggering 80 percent. This massive drop has plunged the region into near-total dependence on international aid just to maintain basic survival.

Widespread destruction of local industry and historic unemployment

The UN document underscores an unprecedented surge in joblessness, noting that formal commercial activity across Gaza has come to a near-total standstill. Widespread damage to arable farmland, manufacturing facilities, and retail networks has effectively eradicated the territory’s productive capacity.

“Standard economic life in Gaza has effectively ceased to exist,” UNCTAD observers noted, emphasizing that the overwhelming majority of families are now entirely reliant on dwindling international relief supplies for day-to-day survival.

Ripple effects across the Palestinian territory and long-term recovery

The economic shockwaves originating in Gaza are severely straining the broader Palestinian economy. Tightened movement constraints, trade bottlenecks, and mounting fiscal pressures continue to cripple business performance and household income across the West Bank as well.

UNCTAD experts cautioned that returning Gaza to pre-conflict baseline conditions will demand a multi-decade commitment from international donors, coupled with billions of dollars in capital investments to restore destroyed residential quarters, water networks, and public utilities.

World.title: Amr Diab secures new Guinness World Record following 69-week reign atop Billboard Arabia charts
World.content:
Egyptian megastar Amr Diab has broken yet another global milestone, securing his second official Guinness World Record after spending a staggering 69 weeks at number one on the Billboard Arabia Artist 100 chart, RT Arabic reported.

The accomplishment cements Diab’s unmatched dominance over the regional music landscape, making him the first Arab artist to sustain a top-charting streak of this scale. In total, Diab has spent 145 weeks on the Billboard Arabia charts, showcasing a rare longevity that bridges classic hits with modern streaming power.

Fan appreciation and evolving sound

Reacting to the international recognition, Diab attributed the achievement entirely to his listener base across the Arab world and beyond.

“My ultimate goal with every new project is simply to connect with the audience and bring them joy,” Diab stated. “Keeping my sound fresh and evolving alongside my listeners is my top priority. Their continued enthusiasm and satisfaction mean far more to me than any numerical record.”

Industry recognition and enduring legacy

Billboard Arabia’s Executive Managing Editor, Juhayna Khalidiah, applauded the historic milestone, emphasizing that Diab’s career represents an extraordinary ability to stay ahead of industry transformations.

“We take great pride in seeing this historic achievement forged right here on Billboard Arabia’s tracking lists,” Khalidiah said. “Amr Diab has done more than just keep pace with changing musical trends—he has consistently led the evolution of Arab pop music.”

This marks the second Guinness World Record in Diab’s four-decade career.

World.title: Iranian airlines cancel all flights to UAE following strict new US sanctions
World.content:
Iranian news agency ISNA reported on Thursday that all flights by Iranian airlines heading to the United Arab Emirates have been canceled effective midnight last night.

This development follows a new package of strict US sanctions on the Iranian aviation sector coming into effect on Wednesday. The Trump administration has pledged to halt all operations of Iranian carriers and impose penalties on any entity engaging in business with them.

The newly enacted sanctions, announced by the Trump administration on Monday as part of a series of measures targeting Iran’s aviation industry, come amid US efforts to escalate economic pressure on Iran.

Concurrently, the Civil Aviation Organization of Islamic Republic of Iran informed local state media that airports in Baghdad and Muscat will also “no longer receive” Iranian flights starting from midnight.

World.title: EgyptAir explains ticket pricing structure
World.content:
Foreign currency accounts for approximately 87 percent of EgyptAir’s total operational expenses, making exchange rates and international costs the primary drivers behind ticket price adjustments, according to Captain Ahmed Adel, Chairman of the EgyptAir Holding Company.

Speaking during a telephone interview on the program El Hekaya (The Story) on MBC Masr, Adel addressed public debate surrounding fare prices, explaining that ticket rates fluctuate based on seasonal demand throughout the year.

He noted that the airline actively mitigates costs for travelers by offering promotional discounts of up to 50 percent during peak travel windows, including year-end and Christmas holiday seasons.

Turnaround to profitability and global rankings

Despite high foreign currency demands, EgyptAir has returned to substantial profitability while advancing in global aviation standings. The national carrier secured 46th place among the world’s top airlines and ranked 20th globally for best cabin crew performance.

“After taking responsibility, I worked to position EgyptAir among the top airlines in the world, and this success was achieved thanks to our dedicated workforce,” Adel stated, attributing the turnaround to employee efforts and support from the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

In-flight telemedicine and passenger volume

The airline currently transports around 11.4 million passengers annually. To enhance passenger safety, EgyptAir has implemented a real-time medical monitoring project. Operating from a dedicated telemedicine room at EgyptAir Hospital, doctors can connect directly with flight crews online to handle in-flight medical emergencies live at 30,000 feet.

World.title: Respecting the dead – Manchester Museum removes Ancient Egyptian Mummy Asru from display
World.content:
After more than two centuries under the public gaze, the Manchester Museum in the United Kingdom announced on Monday that it has removed the ancient Egyptian mummy Asru from the Egypt and Sudan Gallery.

She has been returned to her sealed outer coffin in a move the institution describes as a step toward aligning with her presumed funerary beliefs and spiritual wishes.

Why Manchester Museum took Asru off display

The Manchester Museum clarified in an official statement that its decision was not prompted by a written testament or an explicit message left by Asru herself.

Instead, it was informed by modern Egyptological understanding of ancient burial traditions.

For high-status Egyptians of Asru’s era, the expectation was that their mummified remains would rest indefinitely within protective coffins, fully wrapped and shielded from the eyes of the living.

Re-evaluating these cultural expectations led curators to reconsider the ethics of keeping her body exposed.

Museum officials emphasized that withdrawing Asru from public view reflects a broader shift in how global cultural institutions handle human remains, demonstrating greater accountability and deference to the heritage and sensibilities of source communities.

Who was the ancient Egyptian woman?

Asru lived in southern Egypt approximately 2,700 years ago and was buried in ancient Thebes, near modern-day Luxor.

Hieroglyphic inscriptions on her coffins preserve her identity alongside the names of her parents, including her father, Ba-Kush, who served as a scribe in ancient Egypt.

Her mummified body and ornate coffins arrived in Manchester during the early 19th century after being acquired by merchants William and Robert Garnett, who donated her to the Manchester Natural History Society in 1825.

In April of that year, her linen bandages were unrolled during a public unwrapping event in Manchester—a common practice of the era.

Her body remained on near-continuous display in the city for almost two centuries until museum leadership resolved to return her to her sealed outer sarcophagus.

A person before a museum exhibit

The decision to withdraw Asru coincides with a comprehensive ethical review by the Manchester Museum regarding the stewardship of human remains in its collections.

Throughout 2025, the museum initiated a public dialogue concerning Asru’s future, seeking feedback from visitors while consulting Egyptian researchers and diaspora representatives before reaching a final decision.

Egyptian scholar Marwa al-Hossary of the University of York noted that viewing Asru as a human being who lived and died—rather than a artifact behind display glass—raises critical ethical questions about whether institutions have the right to keep ancestral bodies perpetually exposed.

Is Asru leaving the Manchester Museum?

Removing Asru from public galleries does not mark the final chapter in her journey. She currently rests in her sealed outer coffin within the museum’s climate-controlled storage facilities.

Museum authorities confirmed that her current location is not necessarily permanent as they continue evaluating long-term care frameworks for human remains in their custody.

Future plans may involve creating a dedicated, private space within the museum for her rest, or considering wider discussions regarding repatriation to her country of origin.

For now, after nearly two centuries under museum lights, Asru rests quietly inside her closed sarcophagus, away from the public eye.

World.title: The 2028 presidential race is already here — and it’s early
World.content:
Summer’s swampy heat released its grip on Washington Tuesday as if someone had flipped a switch.

Fall is not the only new season stirring.

The 2028 presidential race, which has long felt like a distant hypothetical amid the wrenching turmoil of President Donald Trump’s early second term, has suddenly sprung into life.

Possible Democratic and Republican contenders are hitting the midterm trail in states that just happen to hold early presidential contests. They’re wading into top policy issues. A few openly yearn for the White House. Some make cryptic comments to keep a door open. Others wonder whether they have a lane.

The sense that a clock is ticking even drew in Trump, who is loath to admit he’s only leasing power. In a UN General Assembly address Tuesday, he reminded his foes in Tehran: “I’ll be here for two and a half years.”

It’s normal for possible presidential candidates to become more visible around this time. Midterm elections offer them cover to engage base voters. They can test new stump lines, assess the political mood, lay down informal early state infrastructure and bank favors with grateful candidates.

But the 2028 campaign suddenly seems more tangible, perhaps because Trump’s fragile political state is inducing end-of-an-era vibes and Democrats have finally stopped mourning the 2024 presidential election.

That debacle was fresh on minds Tuesday when former Vice President Kamala Harris, the party’s last-minute nominee, showed up in Michigan to try to unite Democrats behind Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and former Vice President Kamala Harris participate in a roundtable discussion about reproductive health at Birth Detroit on September 22, in Detroit. David Guralnick/Pool/Getty Images

She’s not the only possible 2028 Democrat making noise. New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has a progressive juggernaut rolling. Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff hasn’t even won reelection, but 2028 buzz is building. Govs. JB Pritzker, Andy Beshear and Josh Shapiro are also on maneuvers.

On the GOP side, every word and gesture by Vice President JD Vance takes on extra meaning as he steels himself for the unfathomable task of a possible presidential run under Trump’s nose. And Sen. Ted Cruz, Sen. Rand Paul and other potential GOP candidates are also openly mulling a run. Even 74-year-old Louisiana Sen. John Kennedy told the Washington Post in an article published Tuesday that while he’s planning on running for reelection, he might take a tilt at the top job “if a bunch of goobers” run for president.

It’s that moment in a nascent presidential season when countless politicians look in the mirror and wonder why not them. At a testing time for US democracy, it’s reassuring that presidential spring training is near.

What each party needs in 2028

The 2028 election, with two open national party tickets, will mark a new political era.

The eventual Republican nominee will have to decide whether there’s a future for MAGA or if the party’s dormant, traditional conservative roots should be revived.

Democrats need someone to unify progressives and moderates. An anti-Trump platform may work in the midterms. But polls show an electorate still sour on a party that lost their confidence when Joe Biden was president.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez arrives before a ceremony to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center at the National 9/11 Memorial & Museum on September 11 in New York City. Adam Gray/Pool/Getty Images

The White House rumor mill slipped into higher gear Tuesday with an intriguing New York Times interview with Ocasio-Cortez. The New York Democrat’s midterm travels are positioning her as the inheritor of Bernie Sanders’ progressive movement. She’s adept at creating splashy viral moments that define Trump-era politics, like her August announcement that she was freezing her eggs.

Ocasio-Cortez, soon to turn 37, told the Times she’s wrestling with the intangible question that can define a presidential campaign. “There’s an argument that some make that this is a very unique political window and, oftentimes in politics, you do only get one shot,” she said. But after two of the last three Democratic nominees were women and both lost, Ocasio-Cortez also seemed to question her ceiling. “I happen to be a woman, and I, you know, happen to be Latina. And I think that there’s a lot of conversation about electability,” she said.

Harris epitomizes such questions. She made her fall debut in one of seven swing states that she lost to Trump in 2024. She has not decided whether to run again.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro addresses supporters at a primary election night rally in Warminster, Pennsylvania, on May 19. Hannah Beier/Reuters/File Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear speaks during an event at the Center For American Progress in Washington on February 19. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/File

But other Democrats are pre-positioning, including a number of governors. Shapiro, who seems to be cruising to reelection in Pennsylvania, last week addressed a pressing national question — whether to place guardrails on artificial intelligence — and condemned Trump’s claim that concerns about the technology’s destructive potential are a “hoax.”

Beshear on Tuesday published a new book, “Go and Do Likewise: How We Heal a Broken Country” — using a classic tactic of heartland leaders who need to build a national profile. “We need to show up in places that we haven’t been in far too long. We need to show up in coal mining communities, in farming communities, and listen to the needs of people,” the Kentucky governor told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on Monday. Asked whether he’d run in 2028, he insisted: “I haven’t made any decision on that.”

Pritzker, of Illinois, has shown Democratic voters he can stick it to Trump. But he’s in the news for a more personal reason after revealing he’s shed 80 pounds on GLP-1 medication. He told CBS News he’s concentrating on his reelection bid and has “not made any decisions about what I might do in the future.”

Another Trump foe, Arizona Sen. Mark Kelly, said at last week’s Atlantic Festival of a possible presidential campaign: “The answer is I might, I just haven’t decided.”

Vice President JD Vance speaks during a news conference in Washington on September 22. Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images

Where does the GOP go after Trump?

Trump has seemed to enjoy jokingly playing off potential heirs like Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But the game will be less fun when he’s a lame duck. The veep is widely seen as a Republican front-runner, and there has been no sign from Rubio that he plans to run. Vance Friday traveled to Iowa, a GOP early state that shows the perils of a presidential campaign. Trump’s unpopularity in a reliable red bastion has left Senate and gubernatorial races surprisingly close.

The vice president’s balancing act and thin record of winning elections in his own right — he was in the Senate for only two years before his current job — explain why he’s unlikely to clear the field.

Former GOP presidential candidate Ted Cruz, who won 11 state contests as runner-up to Trump in the 2016 Republican nominating race, seems to be itching to run again. “It’s no secret that I want to be president,” Cruz said on Texas Lt. Gov Dan Patrick’s podcast in August. He’s not yet made a final decision.

Other possible GOP candidates include Texas Gov. Greg Abbott; outgoing Florida governor and defeated 2024 GOP candidate Ron DeSantis; and Florida Sen. Rick Scott.

Sen. Ted Cruz greets the crowd at a campaign event on September 21 in Houston, Texas. Antranik Tavitian/Getty Images Sen. Rand Paul speaks before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on July 29 in Washington. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/File

Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul, who lost to Trump in 2016, is calling for a free market, anti-tariff candidate to balance Trump-style populism. Will it be him? Paul told the Post he’s 50-50 on making the race.

But maybe there’s a lurker candidate no one has thought of. After all, Trump was regarded as a joke before his anti-establishment takeover of the GOP in 2016. And Democrats seem primed for their own populist takeover.

The name of the next president may not currently be the biggest issue — the midterm endgame and the war in Iran matter more right now.

But when America awakes on November 4, after a late night watching John King call congressional races on CNN’s Magic Wall, the next presidential election will truly begin.

And both parties will increasingly look to a future beyond Trump.

The headline on this story has been updated.

World.title: Liberia: Women Have Not Had Central Role in  War Crimes Court Preparations; A New Project Wants to Change That
World.content:
Women and children carry their belongings through heavy rain near Stockton Bridge in Monrovia in 2003 fleeing fighting between forces loyal to then President Charles Taylor and rebels of the Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy (LURD). Photo: Chris Hondros/Getty Images.

Women have not played a major visible role in recent efforts for postwar justice despite being key targets of much of the violence of the war years. A new project aims to change that by strengthening women’s groups and bringing more women, including young women, into peacebuilding and justice discussions.

Women leaders say they have been discouraged from coming forward to play a more central role in the process by harassment and attacks.

Leaders of the US$3 million project headed by say women should not be seen only as victims of the civil wars. They should also lead investigations, prosecutions, reparations and other parts of the justice, reconciliation and commemoration process.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

More than two decades after Liberian women helped played a decisive role in bringing the country’s civil wars to an end, they have been far less visible in the renewed push to reckon with the wars’ atrocities committed during them.

No woman was shortlisted to lead the Office of the Establishment of the War and Economic Crimes Court of Liberia, and many of the major groups shaping the process are headed by men. Women are involved — including in senior positions and through women-led organizations — but they have been less prominent in some of the key leadership and decision-making spaces.

Women leaders have told FrontPage Africa/New Narratives that they have been reluctant to speak up on the postwar justice process because of attacks and belittling that they have been subjected to in the past.

A new US$3 million initiative is seeking to boost women’s involvement. The project, called the “Gender Promotion Initiative 2.0,” rolled out last week by the Liberian government, the United Nations, Kvinna till Kvinna and other partners, aims to strengthen women’s organizations and bring more women, including young women, into peacebuilding and justice discussions. The three-year project will be implemented in Montserrado, Lofa, Nimba, Grand Gedeh and Grand Cape Mount. The United Nations says more than 40 percent of its resources will go directly to women’s rights organizations.

Mabel M.K. Kear, programme manager at Kvinna till Kvinna, called the initiative “a critical promise that the sacrifices of women and communities will lead to transformation,” adding that reconciliation should be genuine and “peace will be sustained through justice.”

More than 250,000 people were killed during Liberia’s 14 years of civil conflict, according to the United Nations . A 2016 United Nations human rights report said 1.5 million people were displaced inside Liberia or sought refuge in other countries. The report cited a 2005 estimate that 75 percent of Liberian women and girls were subjected to wartime rape.

Liberia’s 2009 Truth and Reconciliation Commission concluded that “women were singled out for abuse simply on account of their gender.” It also found that forced displacement “took a particularly heavy toll on women,” many of whom became heads of their families after losing their spouses.

But women were also central to in ending the fighting. Christian and Muslim women joined forces through the Women of Liberia Mass Action for Peace, staging protests, prayer meetings and other nonviolent actions and taking their demands for peace to negotiations in Accra, Ghana. It was there that they staged a daring threat to undress. This was a cultural signal that the men could not ignore. They swiftly brought the negotiations to a successful conclusion. Leymah Gbowee, as one of the group’s leaders, was later awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for their actions.

Liberian women demanding peace in Monrovia —2003. Credit: Pewee Flomoku.

Asatu Bah Kenneth, was one of those leaders fighting for the end of the war in 2003. Today she is the most senior woman working in the court process as the director of the Office of War and Economic Crimes Anti-Corruption Division. Kenneth also founded and led the Liberia Muslim Women for Peace, which joined the Women of Liberia Mass Action for Peace, whose sustained nonviolent campaign helped pressure Liberia’s warring parties toward peace in 2003.

Women-led groups, including the Female Lawyers Association of Liberia and the Women’s NGO Secretariat of Liberia, are also involved in the current justice process.

That history returned to the international stage this week. The Liberian government held a high-level event on women, peace and security at United Nations headquarters in New York on the margins of the 81st United Nations General Assembly, celebrating women’s historic role in the country’s peace process while calling for greater leadership by women and girls. The event, organized by the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, was held under the theme “From Pioneers to Global Leaders: Liberia’s Journey in Women, Peace and Security.”

President Joseph Boakai used the event to link that legacy to women’s participation in justice today. Launching Liberia’s third National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security, he identified participation and access to justice among its priorities and reaffirmed his commitment to establishing the War and Economic Crimes Court. Boakai used the event to highlight women’s role in national decision-making.

“In Liberia, men make the big decisions, the women make the small decisions, but the women decide which decisions are big and which decisions are small,” Boakai said.

Nobel Peace laureate Leymah Gbowee, who helped lead the Women of Liberia Mass Action for Peace, used the same event to recall how women organized and pushed for peace despite initially being excluded from important spaces.

“Contrary to popular belief that we were a bunch of women who had no strategic direction, we had a direction,” Gbowee said.

Government militia fighters advance during fighting for control of a key bridge in Monrovia in 2003, as forces loyal to President Charles Taylor battled rebels of the Liberians United for Reconciliation and Democracy (LURD). Photo: Chris Hondros

The renewed focus on women’s participation comes at a pivotal stage in the effort to establish the court. Boakai submitted legislation to establish the War and Economic Crimes Court and a National Anti-Corruption Court to the Legislature in May. Weeks earlier, he had renewed the mandate of the Office for the Establishment of a War and Economic Crimes Court of Liberia .

The Legislature is considering competing proposals from the Liberian National Bar Association, a civil society coalition led by the Independent National Commission on Human Rights, as well as Senate President Pro Tempore Nyonblee Karnga-Lawrence and Senator Joseph Jallah .

For supporters of the new gender initiative, the challenge is ensuring that women have a greater role as those decisions are made.

Christine N. Umutoni, the United Nations resident coordinator in Liberia, said the initiative should build on a voice Liberian women have already established rather than treat their participation as something new.

“Liberian women helped end the conflict,” Umutoni said. “So it is not now that we are building the voice.”

The challenge, she said, is ensuring that women’s experiences are reflected throughout the justice process. She warned that “a gender-blind approach would leave serious violations insufficiently addressed and risk weakening public confidence in justice institutions.”

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Investigating Liberia project. Funding was provided by the U.N. Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and the European Union. The funders had no say in the story’s content.

World.title: Liberia: Rep. Jacob Debee Receiving Treatment at Phebe Hospital After Road Accident in Bong County
World.content:
SUAKOKO DISTRICT –Grand Gedeh County’s District Three lawmaker, Representative Jacob Debee, is currently hospitalized after being involved in a road accident along a stretch of highway in Gbondoi Town, located in Yellequelleh District, Bong County.

Following the incident, the legislator was transported to Phebe Hospital in Suakoko District for medical attention, where he remains under care.

Witnesses at the scene say Rep. Debee was en route to the southeastern region of the country at the time of the crash. He was driving a white Toyota Land Cruiser, registration number A-613397, when the vehicle is said to have run off the roadway. Early indications suggest no other vehicle was involved.

It has not yet been confirmed how serious Rep. Debee’s injuries are, nor whether anyone else was riding with him when the accident happened.

As of this report, the Liberia National Police have not released an official account of the crash. Updates are expected once investigators complete their assessment.

World.title: YEIB-MANCO Targets 30,000 Liberian Youth, Moves to Tackle Credit Barriers
World.content:
Monrovia — The Youth Entrepreneurship and Investment Bank Management Company (YEIB-MANCO) is targeting at least 30,000 young Liberians for direct support and another 120,000 indirectly, as it rolls out a financing model aimed at addressing some of the major barriers confronting local entrepreneurs, including high interest rates, stringent collateral requirements and limited access to long-term credit.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

YEIB-MANCO Chief Executive Officer Joseph F. Sando disclosed the targets Thursday during an engagement with journalists in Monrovia, where he outlined the institution’s mandate, financing structure and plans to expand entrepreneurship opportunities across Liberia.

Sando described YEIB-MANCO as a multifunctional institution established through an African Development Bank-backed initiative with the Government of Liberia, with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry serving as a key institutional anchor.

“When anyone hears the word YEIBMANCO, the thing that should register to the mind is sustainable development, sustainable economic development for our country, Liberia, and by extension, Africa,” Sando said.

Despite the word “bank” in its name, Sando said YEIB-MANCO is designed to go beyond traditional lending by combining financing with business development, technical assistance and incubation services.

“It’s a combination of many companies that carry the weight of development in finance, business and incubation,” he said.

Beyond Lending

Sando said YEIB-MANCO remains in its formative stage, with about six people directly working for the institution and nearly 15 when personnel connected to the project implementation structure are included.

However, he said its mandate is nationwide, with a particular focus on young people and women.

Responding about how ordinary Liberians would benefit, Sando said the initiative is designed to reach entrepreneurs across all 15 counties rather than concentrate opportunities in Monrovia.

“To me, in my heart, there is no ordinary Liberian. Everybody in Liberia is an exceptional, extraordinary person,” he said.

According to Sando, beneficiaries will not simply receive financing based on business ideas. Prospective entrepreneurs will first undergo incubation, training and coaching to assess their capabilities and identify sectors where their businesses have the strongest potential.

“You prepare the businessman in all sectors, especially agriculture, and then you take them to the next stage of financing. You give them money,” he said.

“So you’re not just coming to give money to somebody who tells you, ‘Yeah, I can do business.’ You’re preparing and you’re teaching them, you’re coaching them as to how to go about doing the business.”

After financing, Sando said YEIBMANCO would continue monitoring and evaluating beneficiaries and their businesses to assess performance and economic impact.

Three-Pronged Financing Model

Sando said the institution plans to operate through three special-purpose vehicles covering technical assistance and business development services, a guarantee fund and an investment fund.

Under the business development component, entrepreneurs would undergo incubation designed to identify their skills, business interests and appropriate sectors.

The guarantee mechanism, he said, would involve partnerships with commercial banks to address major financing obstacles facing Liberian entrepreneurs, particularly high interest rates, demanding collateral requirements and short repayment periods.

YEIBMANCO could share financing risks with participating financial institutions, Sando said, potentially reducing the collateral burden on entrepreneurs while helping negotiate more favorable interest rates and longer repayment periods.

He illustrated the difficulty faced by entrepreneurs who may be required to provide collateral worth substantially more than the amount they seek to borrow.

“But if I had that money, I wouldn’t come here,” he said.

The investment component would focus on direct coaching and financing in sectors including agriculture, light manufacturing, logistics, technology and recreation.

Sando said the broader objective is to encourage more Liberians to pursue entrepreneurship and reduce heavy dependence on government employment.

He argued that sustainable private businesses could help ease pressure on the public sector, where large numbers of job seekers compete for limited government positions while personnel costs consume significant public resources.

Demand Outpaces Pilot Capacity

Sando said early demand for YEIBMANCO’s business development program has already demonstrated the scale of interest among young Liberians.

According to him, the institution launched a pilot call for applications in August seeking 50 participants for business development services training.

Within the first week, about 300 people had applied, with applications subsequently exceeding 640 for the 50 available slots.

“That tells you how much young people are there outside there waiting, just for that or something to trigger to see how they can go after their success,” Sando said.

He said teams have also been dispatched to Grand Bassa, Nimba and Margibi counties to engage prospective beneficiaries and verify businesses rather than relying solely on documents submitted by applicants.

Sando stressed that transparency and verifiable data would be central to the initiative, saying journalists and the public should eventually be able to independently confirm beneficiaries and businesses supported under the program.

“We want our people to go and interview the beneficiaries, so that tomorrow you people who understand the watchdog, when you come in, we have the data and data is provable,” he said.

$1.03 Billion Financing Gap

On financing, Sando said initial support is coming from the African Development Bank but argued that considerably greater investment will eventually be required to build a vibrant and sustainable micro, small and medium enterprise sector in Liberia.

He cited approximately US$1.03 billion as the level of financing he believes would ultimately be required to strengthen Liberia’s MSME sector, while acknowledging that current resources remain far below that figure.

“So bringing maybe US$10 million, US$15 million, US$20 million, that’s just a drop of water in a mighty ocean,” Sando said. “However, we’re encouraged that at least we have something to start with.”

He said YEIBMANCO is targeting no fewer than 30,000 young people for direct support, with approximately 120,000 expected to benefit indirectly.

While the initiative places particular emphasis on people between ages 18 and 35 and women, Sando said older business owners would not automatically be excluded.

He said businesses owned by older Liberians could qualify if young people constitute about 60% to 70% of their workforce or occupy significant management positions.

The approach, he said, is intended to support not only businesses owned by young people but also enterprises capable of creating meaningful employment and leadership opportunities for them.

Sando thanked the African Development Bank and Liberian government officials and institutions involved in establishing the initiative, saying their collaboration helped create the foundation for the program.

For Sando, the broader ambition is to build businesses capable of creating jobs, generating sustainable incomes and reducing young Liberians’ dependence on government employment.

“We have taken on the challenge that we will lead our people to making sure Liberia becomes second to none in economic development,” Sando said.

World.title: Liberia: Former Ganta Mayor Suah Faces Court Summons Amid Escalating Feud with Chief Justice Gbeisay Over Nimba Land Row
World.content:
GOMPA, Nimba County — A bitter property dispute in Gompa City has widened into a direct clash between the judiciary and local politics, after the Gompa Magisterial Court issued a summons for former Mayor Amos N. G. Suah in connection with remarks he made about Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

Court officials moved to summon Suah after he issued pointed criticism of the Chief Justice’s role in overseeing the disputed land matter, including comments that questioned why Gbeisay had inserted himself into property affairs in Nimba County.

Tensions escalated further when Gbeisay took to the airwaves to defend a controversial eviction and demolition operation carried out in Gompa. He insisted the action stemmed strictly from a magisterial court order and did not represent the Supreme Court acting on its own initiative.

More than 15 households were displaced when structures were torn down or residents were forced out, according to accounts of the operation. Many of those affected have complained that they were given inadequate notice, even as the underlying ownership questions remain legally unsettled.

The case driving the evictions centers on land tied to the estate of the late Musa Toure, pursued through administrator Mohammed Toure against defendants Mohammed Bility and a second individual known as Mr. Dorley. Families connected to the Toure estate contend they have lived on and improved the property for upward of twenty years, arguing that sustained occupation should carry weight against rival paper claims to the land.

The conflict took a sharper political turn when the Chief Justice, during his radio remarks, alleged that Suah had improperly sold public land to private buyers while serving as mayor of Ganta. Gbeisay went on to claim that former Nimba County Superintendent David Door Cooper and the late Senator Prince Yormie Johnson were among those who profited from land deals connected to Suah — allegations that have not been verified through any independent judicial process.

Suah rejected the claims outright. Rather than answering through legal channels, he branded Gbeisay a “security enemy” and publicly urged President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to remove him from the bench. He also challenged whether Gbeisay had genuine ties to Nimba County or any standing to weigh in on its land affairs.

Adding another layer to the controversy, former Superintendent Cooper testified during proceedings before Gbeisay that he and others had already returned a separate parcel of land in Ganta to Suah in an earlier attempt to settle overlapping claims — though it remains unclear whether that parcel has any bearing on the property at the center of the recent evictions.

With the fresh summons, Suah’s public comments about the Chief Justice may now themselves become the subject of judicial proceedings, adding a new legal front to a dispute that has already spanned the courts, the community, and the media.

Gbeisay continues to frame the matter as simple enforcement of a lawful court order, distancing the Supreme Court from direct blame. Suah and affected residents, meanwhile, argue the real issue is how long-term occupants were treated and whether the eviction process was fair. Neither man has been found to have committed wrongdoing by any judicial body, and both sets of allegations remain unproven.

A motion challenging the underlying judgment is reportedly set for a December hearing, leaving the core ownership dispute — and the increasingly personal battle between a sitting Chief Justice and a former mayor — unresolved for now.

World.title: LAA Seeks Aviation Partnerships, Investment at Major African Airports Conference in Nigeria
World.content:
Hughes-led delegation explores technical cooperation, infrastructure support and funding opportunities to modernize Liberia’s airport system

HARBel, Margibi County — The Liberia Airport Authority (LAA) says it is seeking technical partnerships, investment and logistical support to strengthen Liberia’s aviation infrastructure as it participates in a major regional airport conference in Abuja, Nigeria.

The LAA delegation, led by Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Ernest R. Hughes, with Chief Financial Officer Victor Debah, is attending the Airports Council International (ACI) Africa 35th Annual General Assembly, 75th Board and Committee Meetings, Regional Conference and Exhibition, running from September 19 to 25, 2026.

According to a press release issued by the Authority, the weeklong gathering is bringing together airport executives, policymakers, regulators, development partners and aviation industry stakeholders to discuss the future of African aviation under the theme, “Next-Gen Airports: Driving Performance and Resilience.”

The LAA said its participation is intended to strengthen Liberia’s engagement with regional and international aviation institutions while exploring opportunities to improve airport operations, infrastructure and service delivery.

During the conference, the delegation is expected to hold bilateral and multilateral discussions with airport authorities, aviation agencies, development partners, financial institutions and industry stakeholders.

The proposed engagements will focus on technical assistance, operational support, logistics cooperation, capacity development, infrastructure advancement and institutional strengthening.

The Authority said it also plans to explore opportunities for investment, innovation, knowledge transfer and resource mobilization to support the development of Liberia’s airports.

Hughes Pursues Regional Aviation Cooperation

Beyond the ACI Africa conference, Hughes is undertaking separate engagements with key Nigerian aviation institutions, including the Nigeria Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN).

The discussions are intended to strengthen technical cooperation and secure logistical and capital support that could improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of Liberia’s aviation infrastructure.

The LAA said the engagements align with its broader objectives of strengthening aviation safety, advancing airport infrastructure development and building technical partnerships to support the long-term growth of the sector.

The Authority also views the conference as an opportunity to deepen regional integration, exchange best practices with other airport operators and explore emerging technologies that could support Liberia’s aviation modernization efforts.

LAA Links Participation to National Development

The Authority said its participation reflects its commitment to President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s national development agenda, particularly in improving infrastructure, strengthening regional cooperation and expanding transportation connectivity.

ACI Africa, the regional arm of Airports Council International, represents African airports and promotes advocacy, capacity-building, innovation, connectivity and sustainable growth across the continent’s aviation industry.

The LAA said it remains committed to developing a modern, safe, secure, efficient and resilient airport system capable of supporting economic growth, trade, tourism and regional connectivity while improving services for the traveling public.

The press release did not specify the amount of funding or capital support being sought, identify any agreements finalized during the engagements, or provide a timeline for the anticipated infrastructure improvements.

World.title: Liberian Leader Demands Two Permanent African Seats On Security Council, Fairer Global Finance System
World.content:
UNITED NATIONS, New York – President Joseph Nyuma Boakai on Thursday night told world leaders that trust in the United Nations has been broken by the uneven application of its founding principles, and called for sweeping reforms of the Security Council and the global financial system to restore it.

By Rodney D Sieh, rodney,[email protected]

Addressing the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly, held under the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All,” the Liberian leader said the world is facing “a lingering crisis of legitimacy and relevance that demands urgent attention.”

“Our answer to that fragmentation cannot be less multilateralism,” President Boakai declared. “It must be better multilateralism!”

‘Eighty years of patience is enough’

The President reserved his strongest words for the Security Council, noting that Africa, home to 1.5 billion people and nearly one-third of UN membership, still has no permanent seat, even though 80 percent of the Council’s mandates concern African peace and security.

“Eighty years of patience is enough. The time for structural reform is now,” he said, describing the imbalance as a “historical injustice” that “is no longer tenable.”

Reaffirming Liberia’s support for the Common African Position, President Boakai said Africa demands no fewer than two permanent seats with full rights, including the veto for as long as it exists, plus additional non-permanent seats. “Correcting this imbalance is not a favor to Africa,” he said. “It is necessary to restore the United Nations’ trust, credibility, and legitimacy.”

Security Council seat and the drug war

Speaking as a current member of the Security Council, the President highlighted threats facing West Africa, including transnational organized crime, cyber warfare and narcotics trafficking along maritime routes in the Gulf of Guinea.

He said Liberia’s Joint Security forces are “tightening the vise on transnational drug cartels,” but stressed that no nation can fight global criminal networks alone. He appealed to international partners for targeted support in coast guard surveillance, intelligence sharing and port security technology.

He also called for an immediate end to hostilities in conflict zones, unhindered humanitarian access and stronger investment in preventive diplomacy, arguing that “the cost of preventing a war pales in comparison to the cost of rebuilding a broken society.”

‘Governed by so few’

On the economy, President Boakai said developing nations are being “squeezed by unsustainable debt, shrinking fiscal space, and mounting external shocks” as the 2030 deadline for the Sustainable Development Goals approaches.

He called for structural reform of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, whose governance, he said, still reflects the world of 1945. “A financial system that decides the fate of billions cannot continue to be governed by so few,” he said.

At home, he pointed to progress under the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development – focused on Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation and Tourism – citing gains in revenue administration and rural farm-to-market roads. He also said his administration is strengthening accountability, financial management and the fight against corruption.

Climate justice, youth and AI

The President noted that Liberia contributes virtually nothing to global emissions yet suffers coastal erosion, flooding and disrupted farming seasons, while holding 42 percent of the remaining Upper Guinean Rainforest. He urged industrialized nations to honor their climate financing pledges and put loss-and-damage mechanisms into operation.

He called for investment in STEM education and digital skills for Africa’s youth, more than 60 percent of whom are under 25, reaffirmed Liberia’s commitment to equality for women and girls, and joined calls for binding rules on artificial intelligence, particularly in warfare. “Innovation must protect human development, not automate human destruction,” he said.

From San Francisco to today

Recalling that Liberia was one of only four African nations to sign the UN Charter in 1945, President Boakai presented the country’s journey from civil war to constitutional democracy as proof that “institutions can be rebuilt.”

He opened his address by congratulating Khalilur Rahman on his election as President of the 81st Session, thanking outgoing President Annalena Baerbock, and saluting Secretary-General António Guterres as he prepares to end his tenure.

“Let us leave this Assembly committed to a United Nations that not only deliberates on crises but also resolves them,” he concluded.

World.title: Liberia: Kwarbo vs. Coleman: The Drug Van Order that Nobody Owns
World.content:
A statement attributed to detained former Highway Patrol Chief Wadell Kwarbo says IG Gregory Coleman ordered him to escort the drug van. His family denies he made it, and the IG calls it part of a four-month disinformation campaign.

MONROVIA — A few days ago, Wadell Kwarbo’s father appeared on Spoon FM with an account of what his detained son had allegedly told him before he was taken into custody.

By Rodney D. Sieh

According to the father, a senior officer had called Kwarbo and instructed him to escort a shipment of drugs. At the time, he did not publicly identify the officer.

This week, however, a name emerged.

A statement attributed to Kwarbo, the former chief of the Liberia National Police Highway Patrol Division who remains detained at the Monrovia Central Prison, identified Police Inspector General Gregory O. W. Coleman as the officer who allegedly made the call.

“Police IG Gregory Coleman ordered me to escort the van. He instructed me to escort the drugs with my patrol vehicle (RL-141). And I acted on his order,” Kwarbo was quoted as saying on Spoon FM.

The statement reportedly went further, calling for his telephone records and written statement to be made available.

“Let them get my call log. My call log can be subpoenaed through the Court,” he was quoted as saying. “Let them release my written statement also. Why are they keeping it? They have it.”

But there is now a direct contradiction over whether Kwarbo actually made those statements.

Family: “He Never Made Such A Statement”

On Thursday, Kwarbo’s wife, Bendu Kwarbo, issued a statement on behalf of the family distancing her husband from the allegations against Coleman.

The family said it “categorically dissociates” Kwarbo from reports attributing the allegations to him and said neither the family nor his lawyers knew about or authorized any statement accusing the police chief.

“Mr. Kwarbo himself firmly rejects and denies this allegation in its entirety and maintains that he has made no such statement,” the family said.

The family said Kwarbo’s lawyers had advised him to remain silent and allow the court process to determine the case.

It described the statement circulating in his name as “malicious” and urged media organizations and the public to verify information before publishing or repeating allegations.

The family also maintains that Kwarbo should not have been arrested and that the case against him is based on what it described as false and misleading allegations.

Coleman: “Sustained Disinformation Campaign”

Coleman, meanwhile, has rejected the allegation and characterized it as part of what he says has been a prolonged campaign to undermine his credibility.

“For the past four months, I have been the target of a sustained disinformation campaign intended to damage my character and silence my fight against the culture of impunity, including the ongoing drug investigation,” Coleman said.

The police chief said freedom of expression must be respected but warned against spreading what he described as false information concerning an active criminal investigation.

“The facts must be established through evidence and lawful process. Anyone found to have broken the law must be held accountable under that same process,” Coleman said. “I will remain focused on my duty. I will not be intimidated.”

The US$ 317 Million Drug Case

The dispute comes against the backdrop of Liberia’s largest cocaine trafficking investigation, involving a shipment authorities have valued at approximately US$317 million.

Kwarbo, a former Highway Patrol chief, was stripped of his duties and later arrested and charged alongside Anthony T. Blaye, who served as Chief of the Liberia National Police Financial Crime Division.

The two have been accused of using marked police vehicles to escort a large cocaine shipment.

According to findings attributed to a joint Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency and Liberia National Police investigation, the cocaine was transported from a coastal landing site to a stash house using two police vehicles in an escort formation, with one vehicle reportedly positioned ahead of the shipment and another behind it.

Coleman said investigators uncovered evidence indicating that state security personnel played a role in moving the narcotics from the landing site to a holding location.

The foreign nationals, a Serbian and a Colombian, are being accused of bringing the cocaine into Liberia through aircraft and shoreline landing operations.

Liberian authorities publicly destroyed the seized cocaine on July 30 in what officials described as the country’s largest-ever drug destruction exercise.

Kwarbo’s Bail Fight

Kwarbo has denied wrongdoing and, in August, filed a motion seeking bail before Criminal Assizes “C” at the Temple of Justice.

His lawyers, including Cllr. Sayma Syrenius Cephus, maintain that he is being detained largely on allegations that he provided an escort to principal defendants after the alleged crimes had already been committed.

Kwarbo’s lawyers argue that the prosecution has not presented objective evidence placing him at the scene before or during the commission of the alleged offenses.

The defense has also challenged allegations attributed to co-defendant Christian Nyantee, arguing that Nyantee may have a motive to shift responsibility and that uncorroborated accomplice testimony should not be sufficient to establish the legal standard required for continued detention.

Kwarbo’s lawyers further contend that he had no prior knowledge of the alleged drug operation and that providing security escorts can form part of routine security duties during major national-security operations.

The Questions That Remain

The latest dispute leaves several questions unanswered.

It remains unclear who spoke to Spoon FM on Kwarbo’s behalf, whether the statement attributed to him was actually made by him, and how the statement emerged from the prison.

It is also unclear whether the written statement Kwarbo was quoted as referring to exists, what it contains, and whether investigators have sought or obtained his telephone records through the court.

Analysts say those questions may be resolved through evidence presented in court rather than competing accounts outside the courtroom.

For now, the public has two sharply different versions: one attributed to Kwarbo naming Coleman as the officer who allegedly ordered the escort, and another from Kwarbo’s family saying he never made the statement.

Kwarbo remains in detention and, under Liberia’s Constitution, is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction.

World.title: Chipolopolo fall in Algeria
World.content:
Captain Fashion Sakala was on target but Zambia launched the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with a 3-1 loss to Algeria in Group I.

Algeria posted a well deserved win after dominating both halves at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium.

The home side started on a promising note when Jaouen Hadjam opened the scoring just after two minutes.

Algeria went into the half time break leading 1-0 after wasting some decent chances.

Saudi Arabia based Sakala equalised 12 minutes after the break to make it 1-1.

But Algeria bounced back in front after 67 minutes when Ibrahim Maza beat Zambia keeper Willard Mwanza from inside the box.

Winger Anis Hadj Moussa sealed the win in the 72nd minute with Algeria’s third.

The result puts Algeria top of Group I on three points on goal difference after Match Day One, while Zambia are bottom.

In the other Group I match played today, Togo made a winning start with a 1-0 victory over Burundi at the Kégué Stadium in Lomé.

Karim Dermane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to give the Sparrow Hawks all three points.

Togo controlled the first half and held on in the second, with Burundi unable to find an equalizer.

Group I Table After Match Day 1:

1. Algeria – 3 pts (+2)

2. Togo – 3 pts (+1)

3. Burundi – 0 pts (-1)

4. Zambia – 0 pts (-2)

Togo now travel to face Zambia on 29th September, while Burundi host Algeria on the same day.
